entry.title: Learn what makes your business work anywhere with SAP’s mobile apps and AI
entry.content:
Can't wait to check it out? Go directly to the new course

SAP mobile apps with Joule integrationAbout 230 million cloud users worldwide use SAP solutions. SAP's data and business process expertise is unparalleled. However, the possibilities to benefit from this business power everywhere using mobile consumer devices are far from being exhausted by all customers.

A new course on learning.sap.com shows in an easily comprehensible way how to get started with mobile apps from SAP for smart phones, tablets, watches, or mixed-reality headsets.

Discovering SAP's Mobile Experiences is the first version of a learning journey that illustrates why the Joule Work mobile app for iOS app and SAP's AI Copilot Joule are excellent entry points for SAP users in many business environments for using powerful features on simple-to-use mobile devices.

The approximately one-hour-long training offers an overview of all available mobile apps provided by SAP for its solutions, and how managing as well as developing further native apps based on SAP BTP works.

Challenges for businesses, opportunities for mobile applications

With a well-orchestrated mobile setup, getting daily tasks done becomes faster and easier for roles such as supply chain managers, mechanics, engineers, finance managers, and many more. Especially in challenging environments, SAP mobile apps accompany employees with deep AI integration and supporting features for simplified and hands-free operation. With additional AI-driven development possibilities from SAP customers or partners can extend what’s already been offered natively by SAP and even build their own app suites, massively simplified and accelerated by the platform's AI coding capabilities.

All of this, shows the training, makes SAP’s mobile offerings a vital part of any digital transformation strategy.

The first version of Discovering SAP's Mobile Experiences provides separate lessons for the powerful SAP Mobile Start and SAP Service and Asset Manager apps. Further chapters on mobile native apps for business travelers, HR, finance will follow soon.

Discovering SAP's Mobile Experiences is publicly available now and soon also accessible via sap.com/mobile.

entry.title: SAP Mobile Start Troubleshooting Guide
entry.content:
Ensuring a smooth mobile experience is essential for users relying on SAP Mobile Start to access business applications, notifications, and content on the go. But often already during the initial setup that administrators perform – setting up and integrating content into SAP Mobile Start & SAP Build Work Zone – various issues can appear before the app ever reaches end users.

When something isn’t working in SAP Mobile Start, it’s easy to assume the app is the problem. But in reality, most issues come from the surrounding configuration - such as the general service and Identity Provider (IdP) setup, content integration, or how web applications behave inside the mobile in app browser.

In this post, I’ll share my recommendations on how to narrow down where an issue is possibly coming from and highlight the problems & their causes we see most often. Below, I’ll walk you through practical checks you can use to pinpoint and possibly resolve the root cause yourself. And in case a ticket is required, the guidance here should help you provide the right information upfront, speeding up analysis and resolution significantly.

Layers of SAP Mobile Start & How to Detect Where an Issue Comes From 🔎

When troubleshooting SAP Mobile Start, it helps to understand that issues typically fall into one of two areas: the native layer of the app or the web layer of the in-app browser. Knowing which layer is affected gives a good indication of how to continue finding root cause.

1. Native Layer  📱

The native layer covers everything that comes directly from the SAP Mobile Start app itself. This includes:

  • The initial onboarding flow
  • Device registration and connection to SAP Build Work Zone & SAP Mobile Services
  • Native app features such as widgets, push notifications, Spotlight search integration, and app settings
  • Rendering the in-app screens, such as content on the “Start” tab, application tiles, cards and their menu structure on the “Apps” tab or Tasks / Situations on the “To-Do” tab.

If something goes wrong before tapping a tile, there’s a good chance the issue lies in the native layer. Typical examples include a failing onboarding process, errors showing the dynamic values on DynamicAppLauncher tiles, missing tiles or content, or issues related to notifications.

2. Web Layer  🌐

Once a user taps a tile which points to a web application, SAP Mobile Start transitions to the web layer. This means an in-app browser is used inside SAP Mobile Start to open content such as:

  • SAPUI5 / Fiori apps
  • Custom web applications or URLs
  • SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition Workspaces & Pages
  • Any external web-based tool integrated as an application tile

Because these apps run inside an embedded in-app browser, misconfigurations originating from the “web world” often surface here. These may include security related issues (authentication, session handling, 3rd party cookies), the mobile readiness of the integrated applications, or specific environment/integration configurations. Typical symptoms include repeated login screens or apps opening to a blank page.

In-app browser options:
Another topic worth mentioning in the context of the web layer is the in‑app browser options available in SAP Mobile Start. Depending on the platform, two browser types are supported:

  • iOS: Optimized SAP Mobile Start In-App Browser based on the WKWebView (default) and SFSafariViewController (in-app variant of the standard Safari browser)
  • Android: Chrome Custom Tabs (default – provided by the default browser app installed on the device) and WebView

Which browser is used is controlled through feature flags in the SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit for SAP Mobile Start.

SAP Mobile Services - Feature Flags

 This is also where several security features are offered (e.g., clipboard protection, blocking of downloads, etc.) to provide built in Mobile Application Management (MAM) capabilities for the embedded browser environment. These security features rely on the WebView variant, meaning that once any of them is activated, WebView becomes the active browser on both iOS and Android.

On iOS specifically, there is an additional browser feature flag that explicitly sets the WebView based variant, which has an optimized UX for launching Fiori apps in SAP Mobile Start, as the default option. This flag must be disabled if you want to switch to SafariViewController.

I mention this because there are scenarios where switching the browser can be useful - for example, when working with certificate-based authentication, certain Conditional Access policies, or when analyzing web apps that fail to load in the default browser. Testing the same app using the alternative browser option can help isolate whether the issue is browser specific.

For further information on the browser options please refer to our help page: Browser Experience in SAP Mobile Start.


To summarize this section a quick rule of thumb. The issue happens…

  • …before a tile opens the in-app browser? → Native layer.
  • …after a tile opens the in-app browser? → Web layer.

 

General Troubleshooting Steps  🛠

When considering steps for troubleshooting, the above classification of the issue into the native or web layer should be considered. Let’s start with steps to analyze and collect information on issues within the native layer.

Troubleshooting the SAP Mobile Start Native Layer

  1. Re-do the onboarding
    Make sure to log out of the app completely and onboard again. Additionally uninstalling/reinstalling could make sense to assure a clean starting point. Make sure you are using the correct registration QR Code, Deep Link or in case of MDM onboarding, the right parameters. Especially with Deep-Link or MDM-based onboarding, wrong values in these configurations may lead to a failed onboarding flow.

  2. Reproduce the issue on another device / OS
    If possible, test it on a different device on the same platform & on a second device on the other OS compared to where the issue was initially found (iOS vs. Android).
    In similar lines test if the issue affects only specific users or is present for everyone.

  3. Check role and content assignments
    Ensure that the user has the necessary roles assigned to see the content. Also make sure that content is assigned properly to the SAP Build Work Zone site:
    • Roles need to be assigned to the Site & Users
    • Apps need to be assigned to Roles and Groups or Pages
    • Pages need to be assigned to Spaces
    • Spaces need to be assigned to Roles

     Additionally, if content is not appearing in SAP Mobile Start, it might be caused by the fact that the content is not flagged to support the current device form-factor (e.g. phone) or is of an unsupported content type.

  4. Collect logs when required
    SAP Mobile Start supports two levels of logs for further analysis:
    1. Client Logs, which cover deep app functionality like onboarding, native behaviors etc.
    2. Network Traces, that cover connectivity via SAP Mobile Services for e.g. API calls in the native context.

    Both can be very helpful to further narrow down the root cause. Especially when creating a ticket, it’s very helpful for the team to check them and see if any abnormalities surface.

    The upload of Client Logs needs to be enabled inside the Mobile Services Admin Cockpit. Then they can be uploaded via the app’s user menu. Find more information on our Troubleshooting and Support page.

    For the Network Trace the recording needs to be started by an admin inside the Mobile Services Admin Cockpit, you can follow the official documentation. The process is also described under point 2.4 of SAP Note 3582668 - Troubleshooting for SAP Mobile Start.

Analyze the Web Layer Issues in SAP Mobile Start

Once a tile is opened, SAP Mobile Start transitions to the web layer. At this point, content runs inside the in‑app browser (WebView, SafariViewController, or Chrome Custom Tabs depending on platform and feature flags). Authentication flows and SAP Build Work Zone or application configuration come into play.

As mentioned earlier these kinds of issues are what we see most of the time (~80+%) and don’t necessarily directly relate to SAP Mobile Start. The following steps help to further identify whether the issue is originating from outside of the Application: 

  1. Test whether the issue also occurs outside SAP Mobile Start
    This might sound trivial, but many issues we see are reproducible inside a standard or mobile browser. However, they might not show initially as browser behaviors, cookie settings and active sessions keep them hidden.
    1. Open the same content in SAP Build Work Zone on Desktop

      Use a fresh incognito/private window and ensure that 3rd‑party cookies are blocked (this mirrors the default behavior of most mobile browsers – as especially the iOS operating system is very restrictive with 3rd party cookies and cross-domain scenarios). Open the site and the specific application you’re having issues with, and check whether everything behaves as expected. Typical indicators to watch for:

      • Basic Authentication popups ➡️ may indicate failing Principal Propagation
      • Second login screen or error screen when opening a tile  ➡️ often caused by incorrect IdP configuration or differing domains between SAP Build Work Zone and the integrated application
      • Blank Screen ➡️ can be indication that SAP UI5 Version of the backend system is out of maintenance (see also Removing outdated UI5 versions from UI5 CDN - SAP Community and 3001696 - Removed outdated SAPUI5 versions from SAPUI5 CDN - Fiori applications might stop functioning - SAP for Me)

       

    2. Open SAP Build Work Zone in a standalone mobile browser

      If step a. worked without issues, continue by testing the same content in a mobile browser (Safari on iOS, Chrome on Android). Mobile browsers behave differently from desktop browsers and more closely reflect the environment SAP Mobile Start uses internally.
      This helps to verify whether the issue is related to mobile browser behavior, restrictions, or mobile‑specific rendering.

    3. Open the direct application URL

      For the final and most “realistic” test, copy or share the exact application URL from the embedded browser inside SAP Mobile Start. Note that in case you changed security settings the sharing function might be disabled via feature flag.

      This URL will directly open the Application – without the manual navigation action from the SAP Build Work Zone Site - and can reveal differences in authentication or rendering behavior that may not show up during steps a or b. We frequently see incorrect configuration causing that e.g. principal propagation is not correctly working with the SAP UI5 app runtime of the target system when called directly. Such issues are not always appearing when using the SAP Build Work Zone Site on Desktop Browsers, when for example OData requests of dynamic tiles have by chance created a backend session but that is not the case when launching such apps from SAP Mobile Start due to the separate layers.


      If the issue can be reproduced in one of these checks, it is very likely that the root cause lies in the general configuration (e.g., authentication) or in the application itself rather than in SAP Mobile Start app and the configuration itself should be further investigated. If not, the next step may provide additional clues.


  2. Compare behavior between in-app browsers

    Switching between:

    • WebView <> SafariViewController (iOS)
    • ChromeCustomTabs <> WebView (Android)

    and comparing the behavior can be a helpful next step to identify differences in how the in‑app browsers handle your application. In general, the system‑browser variants (SafariViewController on iOS and Chrome Custom Tabs on Android) behave more similarly to standalone mobile browsers, while the WebView may differ slightly or lack certain capabilities. You can switch the browser options as outlined in the “Web Layer” section above. Note that switching the browser will force all users to redo their onboarding! So rather test this before an official rollout or within a non-productive environment.


If none of these checks provide further insights and the issue cannot be reproduced anywhere except inside the in‑app browser of SAP Mobile Start, the final step might be to reach out to the team via the standard ticketing process.

  

Last resort – Creating a Ticket for SAP Mobile Start  📨

After running through the checks above, you should have a much clearer picture of where the issue originates. Maybe you could even figure it out by checking on the general configuration, role assignments, or web content integration.

If you’re still stuck after all this, it might be time to create a ticket — and please, make it a good one! With the information you gathered during these steps, you’re in an excellent position to provide the details we need to analyze the issue quickly and accurately. Here’s what helps us analyze issues faster and more precisely:

  1. A meaningful title
    Avoid generic titles like “SAP Mobile Start not working.”
    Choose something that reflects the actual issue (e.g., “Blank screen when launching Fiori app from Mobile Start on iOS”). This helps support teams quickly differentiate between cases.

  2. The correct support component
    Use the outcome of your earlier checks:
    • If the issue also occurs in SAP Build Work Zone via a browser, it’s likely a SAP Build Work Zone or application configuration topic → consider raising a ticket under the SAP Build Work Work Zone component, find more information on their Getting Support page.

    • If the issue only occurs in SAP Mobile Start, use:
      Component: MOB-APP-SMS

  3. The right priority
    Choose a priority that matches the actual business impact.
    SAP provides clear rules and guidance (see SAP Note on incident priorities).

  4. Technical information
    Include the basics:
    • Device OS (iOS / Android / both) and OS version
    • Installed SAP Mobile Start version (incl. build number)

  5. Detailed error description & reproducible steps
    Be as concrete as possible:
    • Exact steps to reproduce the issue
    • Does it occur always or intermittently?
    • Is it affecting all users/devices or only specific ones?

  6. Helpful attachments
    Visual material is extremely valuable. Attach Screen recordings (best case) or Screenshots. 
    These help us immediately understand what you’re seeing.

  7. A test user
    If possible, provide a dedicated test user.
    This allows the support to reproduce the issue directly and significantly accelerates the analysis.

  8. Steps you already performed
    Summarize what you’ve tested using the guide above. For example:
    • If you suspect the native layer:
      Attach SAP Mobile Start Client Logs + Traces captured while reproducing the issue.
    • If it occurs in the web layer:
      Let us know whether the app works in standalone browsers (desktop, mobile, incognito).

Providing this information upfront not only speeds up the entire support process but also makes it much easier for us to understand where the issue is coming from. The more complete your initial ticket is, the fewer back‑and‑forth clarification steps are needed — meaning you’ll get to a solution faster and with less effort.

Conclusion

I hope this guide helps you get a clearer picture of how to approach troubleshooting in SAP Mobile Start and gives you a solid toolkit for narrowing down issues more quickly. With a bit of structured testing and the right checks, many problems can be identified — or even fully resolved — long before a ticket is needed.

And for those cases where a ticket is the right next step: I’m looking forward to seeing even better, more comprehensive ticket descriptions in the future! 😉 It really does make a huge difference in how fast we can support you.

Thanks for reading, and feel free to share feedback or questions in the comments!

entry.title: Customizing Support Information in Joule Work Mobile app
entry.content:
In today's mobile-first workplace, ensuring users have seamless access to enterprise applications is crucial for productivity and user satisfaction. However, when issues arise, users often find themselves without a clear path to get the help they need.  

Addressing a Critical Gap in User Experience  

One of the most significant challenges organizations face with mobile enterprise applications is the disconnect between users experiencing technical difficulties and the support channels that can actually help them. Users frequently encounter issues such as:  

  • Applications not functioning properly after company-specific setup  
  • Frequent login requirements disrupting their workflow  
  • Missing or unavailable applications they need for their daily tasks  

When these problems occur, frustrated users often turn to channels that aren’t meant for support, such as app store reviews or general feedback forms.  This creates a cycle of frustration that impacts both user adoption and overall productivity.  

To bridge this gap, companies can now add end user support information to the SAP Mobile Start app and configure it in SAP Mobile Services . This enhancement transforms how users can access help when they need it most.  

What Admins Can Customize

Administrators have full control over the support experience in Joule Work mobile app. Here's what you can configure:

  • Company Support Contact Information:  Add up to 3 contact methods for each type:
    • Email addresses for support tickets or direct contact
    • Phone numbers for helpdesk or emergency support lines
    • URLs for support portals, knowledge bases, or ticketing systems
  • Built-In Support Resources: Choose which default options to show or hide:
    • FAQ — General product questions
    • Help — Product documentation
    • Get to know the app — Onboarding and feature guides
  • Custom Support Sections: Add up to 3 custom support entries witch are specific to your organisation and would like the users to see under the Support section in the app:
    • Custom titles 
    • Custom icons 
    • Custom URLs

How to Configure Support Information  🛠

Prerequisites: You must be using SAP Mobile Start version 3.1 or higher.

Support information can be configured through two complementary channels, which can be used independently or together:  

Option 1: Via SAP Mobile Services (Post-Login)  

  1. Open the SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of SAP Mobile Start.
  2. Go to Client Settings → JSON Storage.
  3. Add the userSupportConfig object at the root level of the JSON Storage configuration.

Configuration Structure

The configuration uses a supportItems array, giving administrators fine-grained control over exactly what appears on the support screen — and in what order.

Full Configuration Example:

{
"userSupportConfig": {
"schemaVersion": 2,
"supportItems": [
{
"type": "CONTACT_INFO",
"displayName": "Acme IT Support",
"contacts": [
{ "type": "email", "value": "helpdesk@acme.com", "label": "Email Support" },
{ "type": "phone", "value": "+1-555-123-4567", "label": "Call Support" },
{ "type": "url", "value": "https://support.acme.com", "label": "Support Portal" }
]
},
{ "type": "DEFAULT_FAQ" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_HELP" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_GET_TO_KNOW_APP" },
{
"type": "CUSTOM",
"displayName": "Send Feedback",
"icon": "sap-icon://message-success",
"url": "https://feedback.company.com/joule-work"
}
]
}
}

Support Item Types

  • Contact Information (CONTACT_INFO) - Displays your company's support contact methods. You can add up to 3 contacts per type (3 email addresses, 3 phone numbers, 3 URLs).

  • Built-In Support Options: Include any of the following types in supportItems to surface built-in app features. Labels and icons are handled automatically by the app.

  • Custom Support Links (CUSTOM): Link users to external resources like feedback forms, release notes, or documentation portals. You can add up to 3 custom links.

Configuration Examples: 

Example 1: Contact Information Only

{
"userSupportConfig": {
"schemaVersion": 2,
"supportItems": [
{
"type": "CONTACT_INFO",
"displayName": "IT Support",
"contacts": [
{ "type": "email", "value": "support@company.com", "label": "Email support" },
{ "type": "phone", "value": "+1-555-0100", "label": "Call support" }
]
}
]
}
}
 
Example 2: Contact Information + Built-In Options
{
"userSupportConfig": {
"schemaVersion": 2,
"supportItems": [
{
"type": "CONTACT_INFO",
"displayName": "IT Helpdesk",
"contacts": [
{ "type": "email", "value": "help@company.com" }
]
},
{ "type": "DEFAULT_FAQ" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_HELP" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_GET_TO_KNOW_APP" }
]
}
}
 
Example 3: Complete Configuration With Custom Links
{
"userSupportConfig": {
"schemaVersion": 2,
"supportItems": [
{
"type": "CONTACT_INFO",
"displayName": "Support Team",
"contacts": [
{ "type": "email", "value": "help@company.com", "label": "Email support" },
{ "type": "url", "value": "https://support.company.com", "label": "Support portal" }
]
},
{ "type": "DEFAULT_FAQ" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_HELP" },
{ "type": "DEFAULT_GET_TO_KNOW_APP" },
{
"type": "CUSTOM",
"displayName": "Submit Feedback",
"icon": "sap-icon://message-success",
"url": "https://feedback.company.com/joule-work"
},
{
"type": "CUSTOM",
"displayName": "What's New",
"icon": "sap-icon://document",
"url": "https://help.company.com/release-notes"
}
]
}
}
 

Important Notes

💡Naming Tip: The displayName appears as the support button label on the Settings screen and as the support screen title. We recommend the convention Company Name + Support (e.g., "Acme Corp Support"). Keep all labels short to avoid truncation in the UI.

⚠️No Auto-Translation: displayName and label values are not automatically translated. If entered in English, they remain in English regardless of the user's language setting.

Option 2: Via Mobile Device Management (MDM) – Pre-Login and Fallback  

For organizations deploying SAP Mobile Start through an MDM solution (e.g., Microsoft Intune, VMware Workspace ONE, JAMF), support contact information can also be pushed as part of the managed app configuration. This has two key advantages:  

The support entry is available immediately at app launch, even before the user has authenticated – helping users who encounter issues during onboarding.   It acts as a fallback in the Settings screen when no Mobile Services configuration has been set.  

Add the following keys to your MDM managed app configuration:    

MDM Key  

Description  

com.sap.mobile.joule.displayName  

The support team name displayed to users (e.g., "Acme IT Support")  

com.sap.mobile.joule.support.email  

Support email addresses  

com.sap.mobile.joule.support.phone  

Support phone numbers  

com.sap.mobile.joule.support.url  

Support website URLs  

All fields are optional, but at least one contact method must be provided for the support button to appear.  

Configuration Priority  

When both sources are configured, the following priority applies:  

  • Before login (onboarding screens):  MDM configuration is always used.  
  • After login (Settings screen):  Mobile Services configuration takes priority. If no Mobile Services configuration is present, the MDM configuration is used as a fallback.  
  • If neither is configured:  No support entry is shown.  

This dual-source approach ensures users always have a way to reach IT support, whether they are setting up the app for the first time or using it day-to-day.  

 

Impact on User Experience   📱

Once configured,  users can navigate to Profile and Settings > Support to find all configured support channels and contact information.  For organizations using Mobile Device Management (MDM), support information is displayed prominently on the first screen, even before users complete the onboarding process  

Profile and Settings screen

Contact information Details screen

Mobile Device Management (MDM)

This feature represents a significant step forward in creating a more supportive mobile enterprise environment. Companies can now provide clear, accessible support pathways directly within the mobile experience — fully customized to match their internal support infrastructure.

For IT administrators and support teams, this means receiving support requests through appropriate channels where they can provide meaningful assistance, rather than managing frustrated feedback through app stores or general feedback systems. By controlling what support options appear and how they're presented, IT teams can reduce misdirected requests, improve response times, and create a professional support experience that builds user confidence in the Joule Work mobile app.

entry.title: SAP Mobile Start - Rebranding of the app, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on functionality
entry.content:
SAP Mobile Start - Rebranding of the app, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on functionality 

With the new release V3.0, SAP Mobile Start got rebranded as the Joule Work mobile app, with enhanced Joule integration and advanced single sign-on functionality. 

Rebranding: SAP Mobile Start has been rebranded as the Joule Work mobile app, accompanied by a new app icon and an updated user experience. For customers previously accessing Joule within SAP Mobile Start, the Joule entry point has transitioned from the diamond in the header bar to a full-screen interface that can be accessed via the tab bar. This provides users faster access to Joule.  

All core functionality and features remain unchanged, ensuring continuity for both customers and end users with no disruption to existing workflows.

 Screenshot: Direct Joule access in tab bar

For customers running the Joule Work mobile app within their SAP Build Work Zone environment, existing theming and custom branding capabilities remain unchanged. Customers can continue to apply their current branding configurations without impact.

Enhanced Joule capabilities: With the latest release of the app, Joule Work mobile allows users to dictate their prompts to Joule to allow a fast entry of prompts and a better hands-free experience.

Screenshot: Joule dictation

Single–sign-on:

Currently, users can enjoy a Single Sign‑On–like experience for web content by using the “Remind Me” functionality provided by SAP Cloud Identity Services. With the Joule Work mobile app version 3.0, the app offers an advanced Single Sign-On (SSO) capability, reducing the need for users to manually log in when navigating to trusted web applications in the in-app browser. Please see the following blog go my colleague Thomas Bruckner for details on the SSO topic. 

I hope you will enjoy these new features in the Joule Work mobile app..

entry.title: Joule Work mobile app is here!
entry.content:
So, what is Joule Work? Joule Work provides an AI-based user experience that puts the user into the center; and transforms how users work. With Joule Work, users can express what they want to accomplish, and Joule surfaces the right insights, automates routine work, and coordinates AI agents across systems to achieve it – all in one dynamic workspace, on the desktop as well as on mobile. Joule Work acts as an engagement layer that spans across SAP products and beyond and coexists with current experiences provided by pre-defined application UIs. 

Our first version of the Joule Work mobile app comes with two main elements: Conversations and Space.
Let have a look the at the two.

Conversations are AI powered chats with role-based intents, conversation threads, and dynamic response types. Conversations are the main way to interact with the system, users can articulate their needs in a certain context, and Joule will take the required actions or provide the right answers.
The Joule Work mobile app also allows users to have hands-free voice conversations with Joule what is very helpful while being on the go. 

 

 

Screenshot: Conversations, Conversation with context and voice mode

Spaces are dynamic, intent-driven workspaces for more complex business problems. They are composed in real time to bring the right data from different systems, tools, and context together for a specific goal, freeing people from working in multiple applications and passive UIs.​ With the Joule Work mobile app, users can work with their spaces while being away from their desk.

Screenshot: Spaces

entry.title: Seamless Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On with the Joule Work mobile app
entry.content:
With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start) introduces a feature that many customers have been asking for: seamless Single Sign-On when opening web applications in the in-app browser. In this post I want to explain the problem this feature solves, how it works conceptually, and what administrators need to configure to enable it.

The Problem: Two Sessions, One App Experience

Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start), when connected to SAP Build Work Zone, is the native mobile entry point for the Intelligent Enterprise. From a single app, users can access native features like widgets, push notifications, and smartwatch complications, but also launch web applications directly from the app – for example SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA, collaborative Workspaces in SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, custom extensions build on the SAP Business Technology Platform, and more.

When a user taps on a tile that opens a web application, the Joule Work mobile app instantiates the in-app browser provided by the mobile operating system – iOS or Android. This is a technical context switch: the native application session, which is managed by SAP Mobile Services and backed by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, is logically separated from the browser sessions of web applications, for example SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition.

As a result, the in-app browser may not have a valid session for the target web application when launched. The user is redirected to the identity provider and prompted to log in again. This is particularly jarring because, from the user's perspective, they are just navigating within their app.

The Previous Recommendation – and Why It Was Not Ideal for all customers

Customers could avoid this by enabling the "Remember me" functionality of SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This feature creates a long-living session cookie in the browser, keeping users signed in across browser sessions for a configurable duration. A similar capability exists on many corporate identity providers (third-party IdPs) to which SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication may be configured delegating the actual authentication. Long-lived cookies on these providers effectively keep the user session alive in the in-app browser in the same manner.

However, this approach has a fundamental drawback: long-lived session cookies are not ideal and may not be wanted to be generically configured on the company's Identity Provider. Furthermore, "Remember me" only prolongs the time until a user is asked to sign-in again in the in-app browser – it is not fully getting rid of it.

Another alternative that some customers consider is password-less sign-in using client certificates. While this is a genuinely secure and, once set up, a convenient approach, it is not feasible for all customers and all users. Client certificates typically require an active Mobile Device Management (MDM) system to push certificates to managed devices – meaning unmanaged devices, common in bring your own device (BYOD) environments, are excluded. Beyond the deployment challenge, mobile operating systems restrict access to the system keychain for third-party apps, so not all in-app browser variants can reliably make use of client certificates. Other password-less options such as FIDO passkeys or biometric-based flows can require some form of manual user interaction during authentication, which breaks the seamless experience users expect when tapping a tile in the app.

The New Solution: Mobile-to-Web SSO

With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app introduces a dedicated Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On flow that bridges the native session and the in-app browser – securely, without requiring long-lived cookies. Here is how it works conceptually:

The mobile app already holds a valid session with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (in the context of SAP Build Work Zone, to which the app is connected to). The SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant generally serves as the trust anchor for both SAP Build Work Zone, the native app and other SAP and non-SAP solutions including web applications exposed to SAP Build Work Zone. This shared trust is what makes it possible to bridge the two worlds: because both the native app session and the target web applications are anchored in the same SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant, it can act as a secure intermediary, translating the native session into a web session in the in-app browser without requiring the user to authenticate again.

When the user opens a web application in the in-app browser, the app first exchanges its active native session for a short-lived, one-time use SSO token issued by SAP Cloud Identity Services. This token is valid for only a very short time and can only be used once by the mobile app for (re-)establishing a session in the in-app browser on the mobile device.

This is done by passing this one-time SSO token to SAP Cloud Identity Services within the browser context. The SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the token, maps it to the user's identity & native session, and establishes a regular web session – setting the standard browser session cookies. From there, the accessed target web application authenticates against SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication transparently via its standard SAML or OIDC flow reusing the established IAS session with no user interaction required.

The key properties of this approach:

  • Security-friendly: The SSO token is a one-time use token with a short validity. There are no long-lived session cookies involved on the identity provider side.
  • Admin-controlled: The feature can be controlled via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of the Joule Work mobile app. The administrator also defines exactly which web applications are trusted for this flow by configuring them in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • Broadly compatible: The feature works with all in-app browser variants offered by Joule Work mobile app on iOS and Android. It also works with all web applications – SAP solutions as well as custom or third-party apps – as long as they share a common SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication tenant with the environment the mobile app is onboarded to.

Key Prerequisite: SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as the Common Trust Anchor

For the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow to work, SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication must be the identity provider for both the native mobile application and all web applications that should benefit from seamless SSO. The trust is established and maintained through SAP Cloud Identity Services, making it the single common denominator across all participants.

It is important to clarify that SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication does not need to be your end users' primary authentication system. In many enterprise landscapes, SAP Cloud Identity Services acts as an identity proxy, delegating the actual authentication to a corporate identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID or other identity providers. This is fully supported. The only requirement is that SAP Cloud Identity Services is the first common trust anchor in the chain – meaning all participating web applications are configured to trust it directly, even if it in turn proxies to a corporate IdP.

One configuration detail to be aware of in proxy setups: the "Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP" setting in SAP Cloud Identity Services must not be enabled for the applications involved in the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow. When this setting is active, SAP Cloud Identity Services bypasses its own session handling and always redirects to the corporate IdP – which would cause the Mobile-to-Web SSO token to be ignored, and users would end up with a login prompt again. Beyond Mobile-to-Web SSO, enabling this setting can also cause issues in iFrame-based in-place app integration scenarios, as corporate identity providers frequently block iFraming to protect against clickjacking and similar attack vectors. For more information on this setting, see Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP (SAP Help).

The trust for the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow is configured explicitly in SAP Cloud Identity Services. The administrator defines which web application entries in SAP Cloud Identity Services are allowed to participate in this flow – only applications that have been explicitly added to the trust configuration can benefit from it. In addition, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs configured for the trusted application. This means a web application can only receive a seamless SSO session if its URL matches one of the permitted redirect URI patterns. Both aspects – the application trust list and the redirect URI validation – ensure that the administrator retains full control over which applications can be reached via this mechanism.

Please note: Customers with SAP Build Work Zone subscriptions created before March 2025 may not yet be using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication directly. For these environments, it is necessary to explicitly switch the authentication mechanism. Subscriptions created after that date are automatically set up with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. Please refer to the SAP Help documentation for the migration steps: Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.

Pro tip: As with other features that depend on shared sessions and cookies – such as the iFrame-based in-place integration of web applications – it is important that all components share a common super domain. We strongly recommend operating SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication and your SAP cloud solutions under the SAP Common Super Domain cloud.sap, while other domains work as well as long as they are aligned across the stack to prevent cross-domain restrictions. If you are not yet familiar with this topic, our earlier blog post explains the background and the configuration steps in detail: Demystifying the Common Super Domain for SAP Mobile Start.

Which Web Applications Are Covered Automatically?

When Joule Work mobile app is connected to SAP Build Work Zone, both share the same Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This means that SAP Build Work Zone itself is automatically within the trust scope – no additional configuration is needed for it.

This automatic coverage includes for example:

  • SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition Workspaces – collaborative workspace content embedded in the Work Zone experience
  • Custom extensions hosted on SAP BTP – applications built for example with the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model, deployed to the SAP BTP and served using the Approuter of SAP Build Work Zone. (For details on building such extensions, see Building Pro-Code Extensions for SAP Mobile Start)
  • SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA On-Premise or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition running through an SAP Cloud Connector using a Principal Propagation Destination – these are tunneled through the BTP subaccount and are therefore covered by the same Application entry

The key distinction is that automatic coverage applies to applications that are part of – or tunneled through – the SAP BTP subaccount and its corresponding SAP Cloud Identity Services Application. Applications that run on their own infrastructure and have their own independent trust relationship with SAP Cloud Identity Services are not automatically covered, regardless of whether they are launched in embedded ("in-place") mode or opened directly ("ex-place"). A prominent example is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: even when it is iFramed within the SAP Build Work Zone shell, it has its own Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services and must be explicitly added to the Native-Web Trust group.

For all such web applications – SAP solutions with their own IAS Application entry, third-party apps, or any app not part of the Work Zone BTP subaccount – administrators add them to the trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as described in the setup steps below.

Administrator Setup

Step 1: Verify That IAS-Based Authentication Is Active

Before enabling the feature, confirm that SAP Build Work Zone is using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as its identity provider. If this is not yet the case, follow the migration steps referenced in the prerequisite section above.

Step 2: Enable the Feature Flag in SAP Mobile Services

In the SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit, navigate to the Client Settings. In the Feature Flags section, locate the entry named "MobiletoWebSingleSign-On" and activate it.

Screenshot showing the highlighted feature flag in the activated state in the Mobile Services Admin Cockpit.

For reference, the corresponding documentation can be found here: Single Sign-On for Web Apps – SAP Help

Step 3: Add Trusted Web Applications in SAP Cloud Identity Services

For web applications that are not automatically covered through the SAP Build Work Zone application (see the previous section), you can add them to the trust configuration:

  1. Sign in to the administration console for SAP Cloud Identity Services.
  2. Go to Applications & Resources → Applications.
  3. Select the application entry that corresponds to your SAP Build Work Zone instance.
  4. Go to the Trust tab, then navigate to Application APIs → Dependencies → Native-Web Trust.
  5. Click Add and select the application with which you want to establish trust.
  6. Save your selection.

Screenshot of SAP Cloud Identity Services to maintain Native-Web Trust Settings

Users opening applications from this trust list in the in-app browser will now benefit from the seamless Mobile-to-Web SSO flow.

Step 4: Verify the Redirect URIs of Trusted Applications

As described in the prerequisite section, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs of the trusted application entry. For SAP-delivered solutions – such as SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – the redirect URIs are typically pre-configured correctly by SAP and no further action is needed.

However, for custom-built applications or third-party web apps that rely on the general SAP Business Technology Platform application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services, you should verify that the application's URL is covered by the configured redirect URI patterns. If the URL does not match any permitted pattern, the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow will not complete successfully for that application.

You can review and adjust the redirect URIs in the SAP Cloud Identity Services administration console under the application's configuration. For the rules and wildcard syntax supported for redirect URIs, refer to the SAP Help documentation: Redirect URIs and Post Logout Redirect URI Rules (SAP Help).

Summary

With the Mobile-to-Web SSO feature, Joule Work mobile app version 3.0 closes the session gap between the native app context and the in-app browser – cleanly, securely, and with full administrator control.

Key takeaways:

  • The feature eliminates the need for long-lived "Remember me" cookies on the identity provider, which are a security concern and not universally available.
  • It is based on short-lived, one-time use SSO tokens issued and validated by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, which acts as the common trust anchor.
  • The feature is optional and in control by the customer: an administrator (de-/) activates it via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of Joule Work mobile app and controls which web applications participate via the Native-Web Trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • SAP Build Work Zone web UIs and tunneled embedded business apps are automatically covered. Additional apps can be added with a few clicks.
  • The feature is compatible with all in-app browser variants in Joule Work mobile app and all trusted web applications, regardless of whether they are SAP solutions or custom apps.

If you need further assistance configuring and making use of this new feature in the Joule Work mobile app, feel free to contact our product management team using jouleworkmobile@sap.com, which will be able to suggest the next steps for your scenario.

Further Reading

  • Joule Work mobile app – Single Sign-On for Web Apps (SAP Help)
  • Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (SAP Help)
  • Demystifying the Common Super Domain for SAP Mobile Start (SAP Community Blog)
  • Building Pro-Code Extensions for SAP Mobile Start – Leveraging Mobile Native Features (SAP Community Blog)
  • SAP Mobile Experience Community Page

entry.title: What’s New in SAP Build: Q1 & Q2 2026 Release Highlights
entry.content:
Greetings, Builders! We blinked and just like that, the first half of 2026 is complete. There’s been a whirlwind of updates, including our recent announcement at SAPPHIRE of the new Joule Studio for intent-based development and agent creation.

Q1 and Q2 also brought a wave of innovations across SAP Build, helping our users extend and automate applications faster than ever. From AI-powered capabilities in SAP Build Work Zone, Joule Work Mobile, CAP, and SAPUI5, to improved visibility in process automation and more, these enhancements address some of your key pain points around developer productivity, simplified workflows, and user experience. Here are the Q1 and Q2 2026 release highlights from SAP Build, plus a look ahead at the new Joule Studio and how you can start learning the fundamentals of AI Agent building today.

Improved Customization and Gen AI in SAP Build Work Zone

No, it's not a social networking site from 2003, it's personalized, relevant SAP content.

Easy access to personalized content with My Space

Following the clear feedback from customers, it’s now possible to organize and manage your favorite Work Zone content on a dedicated, personal page. Many business users often have multiple roles, which may include content spanned across various spaces and structures. The “My Space” capability lets you bring all of that together on one page, allowing you to quickly access your relevant content and easily edit it to fit your specific needs.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @ThomasHensel

Enhanced text generation and refinement with AI

The text widget toolbar now includes an AI option to generate text for the widget. In addition, AI can refine the text in input fields, text areas, and text widgets. This includes changing the tone of the text, adjusting its length, and fixing spelling and grammar.

Create whole workspaces, locate relevant content and more with Joule

At the end of last year, Joule became integrated into SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, bringing the AI assistant’s conversational intelligence right to your workspace. Now, Joule supports three new, frequently used scenarios:

  • Transactional: Create workspaces based on templates, upload content, or invite users to become members.
  • Navigational: Search for specific workspaces that you manage or are related to keywords.
  • Informational: Search for a specific user and show their profile.

You can trigger each of these scenarios through the familiar conversational experience with Joule, executing more tasks and finding key information faster.

👉 See example prompts and learn more on the Help Portal.

👉 See all the latest releases from SAP Build Work Zone.

Updates in Mobile: Seamless SSO, end-user support, MDK 26.6 & more

SAP Mobile Start’s rebranding, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on

SAP Mobile Start has been the established native mobile entry point for your company’s systems and daily tasks, including content from SAP Build Work Zone. The app has now been rebranded as the Joule Work mobile app. While the core functionalities remain the same as before, the new app includes an updated Joule icon, full-screen interface, and voice dictation of prompts. 

With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app also introduces a streamlined single sign-on for opening web applications in the in-app browser. For organizations with large mobile workforces, this eliminates the need for repetitive credential entry and creates a seamless workflow across applications. Learn more about these updates in the blog posts by @ThiloBerndt and @thomas-bruckner.

  • SAP Mobile Start - Rebranding of the app, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on functionality
  • Joule Work mobile app version 3.1 is out
  • Seamless Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On with the Joule Work mobile app

Customizing in-app support for end users in Joule Work

Getting technical support for mobile app issues is a common frustration that often causes users to turn to the wrong channels, such as app store reviews or generic feedback forms. It’s now possible for companies to add support information, such as contact details, ticketing systems and resources, directly to your Joule Work mobile app and configure it in SAP Mobile Services. This enhancement transforms how your end users can access help when they need it most.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @ivan_chaushev.

AI feedback forms, extended compliance checks and more in MDK Client 26.6

The latest release of Mobile development kit (MDK) is now available, bringing several significant upgrades to security, compliance and embedded AI in native mobile app development. Device compliance checks have now been extended to before a user onboards, allowing for earlier detection of compromised devices and stronger security. Enhancements to AI are also ongoing, including a new control that enables quick user feedback on AI-generated content.

👉 See the complete list of new MDK features in this blog post by @Jitendra_Kansal.

New CAP plugins for AI recommendations & improved traceability

RPT-1 generated recommendations with CAP AI plugin for node.js 

In pro-code development, SAP Cloud Application Programming (CAP) continues to provide productivity gains by allowing developers to reduce boilerplate code and focus on problem solving. The new SAP CAP AI plugin for node.js provides recommendations powered by RPT-1 within the in-app UI. The plugin supports multi-tenancy, simplifies AI Core configuration, and inherently embeds the enterprise readiness of CAP out-of-the-box.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @rupamaity.

New and improved change tracking plugin

Version 2.0 of the change tracking plugin for CAP has been released and brings major improvements to how enterprise applications capture and visualize data changes. The new version includes tree table visualization, support for CDS Expression Language (CXL), and a fundamentally redesigned architecture. These changes bring significant upgrades to performance and traceability, allowing developers to exercise more control over changes and customizations.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @rupamaity.

Streamlined SAPUI5 development with AI and developer extensibility

UI5 plugins for modernization and coding agents in GitHub Copilot

Keeping your SAPUI5 app up to date just got easier. The new UI5 Modernization Plugin automates the most time-consuming parts of app modernization: replacing deprecated APIs, eliminating global namespaces, and much more. The plugin is available for Claude Code as well as GitHub Copilot. Also now available for GitHub Copilot are UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents (previously known as UI5 Plugins for Claude). These bring up-to-date SAPUI5 knowledge directly into your AI-assisted development workflow.

The latest version of the UI5 MCP Server is also now available and supports the development of UI Integration Cards. It includes three new tools to assist Large Language Models (LLMs) in creating new cards from scratch or editing existing ones, following the best practices for card development. Learn more about these plugins:

  • Introducing the UI5 Modernization Plugin: Modernize Your OpenUI5/SAPUI5 App in Hours, Not Weeks
  • UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents: Now Supporting GitHub Copilot
  • UI5 MCP Server Got Extended for UI Integration Cards Generation

Key User Adaptation & Transitions for UI5 TypeScript developers

With key user adaptation, business users can change the UI of SAP Fiori standard apps directly in the runtime app. If more complex changes are needed, there now is a seamless transition from key user to developer extensibility in SAP Build.

TypeScript is going through its biggest transition in years. If you build SAPUI5 applications with TypeScript, we have provided a guide for developers around these changes.

👉 Learn more about key user adaptation and the TypeScript transition.

Extended visibility and proactive monitoring in process automation

Avoid manual error-tracing with automated exception handling.

Enhanced process visibility with instance-level attributes

Operational teams often lack business context in process monitoring. For a business user, this can make it difficult to see key details like approaching deadlines or decisions taken by the previous approver. Now with more instance-level attributes enabled: Active Step - Upcoming due date and Last Step Outcome, you can add more meaningful context to process instances, allowing users to easily search, filter, group, and analyze processes where a step is due soon. This allows teams to improve their decision-making and reduce the risk of breaching SLAs.

👉 Learn more about instance-level attributes in the Help Portal.

Process group connections & other updates

More updates are now available in process automation, focused on improved visibility, proactive monitoring, and enhanced governance. Here are some highlights:

  • Process group connections (1-to-many): Organizations often need visibility across related processes, not just individual workflows. This enables end-to-end monitoring by linking a primary process with its associated downstream processes, providing a more complete view of business execution.
  • Notifications in Visibility Scenarios: Proactive email alerts notify users about processing failures, skipped instances, or event thresholds before they impact operations. This reduces manual monitoring and helps teams respond to issues faster.
  • Environment Filters: New controls allow users to view or restrict process visibility by environment. This improves governance and makes it easier to manage and analyze process data across development, test, and production landscapes.
  • Event handler to catch Action errors: Introduces configurable Retry mechanisms and structured exception handling at the Action level. This allows organizations to systematically manage errors, while reducing manual and time-consuming troubleshooting efforts.

👉 See all the latest releases and documentation on the Help Portal.

Looking ahead to the new Joule Studio

If you're looking to learn more about the new Joule Studio and how you can use it to start creating AI agents, we have great news: the learning journey Introducing Joule Studio is now available! With this free course, you'll be able to understand the bigger picture and how Joule Studio fits into SAP Business AI Platform. You'll also get to know what you can do with Joule Studio and Joule Work, how you can use it to create agents and automate workflows with n8n.

👉 Start learning today: Introducing Joule Studio

entry.title: SAP UX Q3/2026 Update – Part 1: AI, Joule, Mobile, SAP Build Work Zone
entry.content:
This series of posts gives an overview of user experience innovations in the public cloud from the last six months, covering our whole portfolio, such as AI and Joule, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608, SAP SuccessFactors etc., as well as innovations in our UI technologies for building great UX.

In this first post, we’ll look at the latest cross-suite UX innovations from Joule and Joule Work, including Joule Work mobile, and SAP Build Work Zone.

Here are the links to the other posts in the series published so far:

  • Part 2: SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition 2608
  • Part 3: SAP SuccessFactors
  • Part 4: SAP Fieldglass
  • Part 5: SAP Concur
  • Part 6: SAP LeanIX
  • Part 7: SAP Analytics Cloud
  • Part 8: SAP Signavio
  • Part 9: UI Design and Technology for Web and Mobile

Before we get started: if you haven’t already seen them, do have a look at the overview of public cloud UX innovations I posted in Q1/2026 (parts 2 to 9 are linked in part 1):

  • SAP UX Q1/2026 Update – Part 1: AI, Joule, SAP Build Work Zone, SAP Mobile Start.

This upcoming series of posts includes Joule and AI UX highlights from individual products within the SAP Autonomous Suite, but for a more comprehensive overview of our recent AI innovations, not just UX related, have a look at:

  • SAP Business AI: Release Highlights Q1 2026.
  • SAP Business AI: Release Highlights Q2/2026.

Joule and Joule Work

With Joule Work we provide AI-native engagement layer experiences, which complement existing application experiences. Have a look at my blog post from May to get an overview of what it means for you:

  • SAP UX Update: The New Joule Work Engagement Layer Experiences

As stated there, it is initially only available to selected customers for Early Adopter Care (EAC). The registration for this is now closed.

Joule Work Desktop

In addition to web and mobile access to Joule Work, we now also provide Joule Work Desktop, which customers participating in the EAC program can install on Apple Mac or Windows computers.

Figure 1: Joule Work Desktop. Alt Text: A laptop screen showing Joule Work Desktop, with a list of conversations on the left quarter of the screen, and on the right “Good afternoon, Alex” above a text entry field containing light gray text “How can I help you?”

With Joule Work Desktop, users have access to local data and skills. This is particularly useful for developers, using the Joule Work Develop experience provided by Joule Studio. With Joule Work Desktop you can generate presentations, summaries, and more based on local data, skills and MCP servers. It enables you to streamline repetitive tasks using your own skills or those skills provided by your company.

You can have it search in the web search as well as in your e-mails. It lets you access MCP for SAP and non-SAP systems, in a secure, authenticated and compliant manner.

Multi-system support for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Editions

Joule now supports connecting multiple SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition systems or clients within a single Joule formation. It also supports connecting multiple SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition systems.

As a result, users who work with multiple systems can use Joule to access data and insights and execute processes in these systems.

Further Information on Joule

If you want an overview of what’s new, or want to set up Joule in your landscape, have a look at these regular blog posts from Shanna Bauer, or look at the documentation:

  • From Hype to Hands-On: Level Up Your AI Skills This June (this sign-up link gives you access to recordings on demand).
  • Joule documentation (including What’s New, integration guide and more).
  • Joule overview (PDF file).

For an overview of what is planned, have a look at the road map for Joule in the SAP Road Map Explorer:

  • Joule Road Map.

 

Joule Work Mobile App

As I outlined in my blog post on Joule Work, Joule Work mobile app includes the functionality previously provided by SAP Mobile Start and extends it. Currently, it offers two experiences, depending on the backend to which it is connected:

  • SAP Build Work Zone experience – when connected to SAP Build Work Zone. My blog post gives an overview of new capabilities introduced with the first release of the Joule Work mobile app (which has release number 3.0).
  • New Engagement Layer experience, when connected to Joule Work – currently only available to customers in the EAC program. My blog post shows what it looks like.

For the SAP Build Work Zone experience, the latest 3.1 release lets you directly access workspaces from SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, via a new entry in the navigation bar at the bottom of the screen. Selecting this brings up a screen showing a list of workspaces, with options for showing your favorites, recently visited etc. – as shown in Figure 2.

Figure 2: Use Joule Work mobile app to access workspaces from SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition. Alt Text: Image of a mobile phone showing three workspaces listed. Buttons for “Favorites”, “Recently Visited” and “Recent Activities” at the top. The bottom row has five navigation icons with text “Start”, “Joule”, “Workspaces”, “Apps”, and “To-dos”.

Also, users can now change the language of external SAP Build Work Zone tiles, like news and to-dos directly inside the app, from the settings screen.

For the Joule Work new experience, users of the 3.1 release can pin their favorite Spaces to the top of the list of Spaces.

Voice for Joule Work Mobile App

Currently also only available to select customers via an Early Adopter Care program which is already fully signed up. Voice for Joule lets you use real-time voice capabilities in Joule, greatly enhancing the user experience.

Find out more

Find out more about all these 3.1 release enhancements, as well as the roadmap, here:

  • Joule Work mobile app Version 3.1 is out.
  • Joule Work mobile app for Android roadmap.
  • Joule Work mobile app for iOS roadmap.

SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition

Personalization Enabled

I am pleased to inform you that we now provide a much-requested capability for SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition: you can personalize the user experience via the new “My Space” page.

We give you an easy-to-use WYSIWYG editor that allows you to easily organize & manage your favorite Work Zone content on a dedicated, personal page. This helps increase your productivity by giving you:

  • Quick access to your favorite content such as apps or UI cards;
  • Convenient access to your “My Space” on desktop and mobile devices.

Figure 3 shows an example of a personalized My Space page, and figure 4 shows what the WYSIWYG editor looks like.

entry.title: What AI Adoption Looks Like Through the Lens of Information Security 🔐
entry.content:
🔐Trust Over Speed: What AI Adoption Looks Like Through the Lens of Information Security

⏱️ Read Time: 4 Minutes

🚀As organizations race to embrace AI, a familiar tension is emerging: the business wants to move fast, while security teams are focused on managing risk. In a recent conversation with Sebastian Haupt, VP of Information Security and SaaS Operations at Pager Health, one message stood out above all others: the AI race won't be won by speed alone. It will be won by trust.

While businesses see AI as a pathway to greater productivity and efficiency, security leaders are increasingly being asked to answer a critical question: How do we innovate responsibly without exposing the organization to unnecessary risk? 🔍

🤖AI Adoption Is Moving Faster Than Any Previous Technology Wave

📈Unlike cloud computing or previous waves of enterprise technology, AI has arrived with unprecedented visibility. Employees are discovering AI tools through social media, personal assistants, and consumer applications long before IT or security teams have evaluated them. The result is significant pressure on organizations to adopt AI quickly.

Yet despite the enthusiasm, many organizations remain in experimentation mode. Employees are testing capabilities, but few have fundamentally transformed their daily work processes. This creates a gap between executive expectations, business demand, and organizational readiness. 🚦

The challenge is no longer whether AI will be adopted. The challenge is how to adopt it effectively and safely.

🛡️ Security's Role Isn't to Say No. It's to Get to Yes.

💡One of the strongest themes emerging from the discussion was the evolving role of information security.

Historically, security teams have often been perceived as the department that slows initiatives down. According to Haupt, that approach is no longer viable. Simply saying "no" does not reduce risk. It often drives employees toward unauthorized tools and workarounds, creating even greater exposure through "shadow AI."

Instead, security must become a business partner focused on enabling responsible adoption. This means evaluating AI vendors, understanding data-use rights, assessing subcontractors and AI service providers, and establishing guardrails that allow innovation to continue safely. ✅

Organizations that create open conversations between business leaders and security teams will be better positioned to unlock AI's value while maintaining trust.

📂AI Doesn't Create Data Problems. It Exposes Them.

🔦One particularly compelling insight was the idea that AI often acts less like a disruptive force and more like a spotlight.

Many companies have existing issues with permissions, access controls, and data governance that have remained hidden for years. AI-powered enterprise search and assistants can suddenly surface information that was previously difficult to find. What looked secure may simply have been undiscovered.

For example, a sensitive document buried deep inside a shared folder may have incorrect permissions. Employees never noticed because nobody could easily find it. With AI, a simple question could expose it instantly.

The lesson is clear: before scaling AI initiatives, organizations should strengthen foundational capabilities such as:

  • 🔑Identity and access management
  • 📊Data governance
  • 🏷️ Data classification and tagging
  • 🔒Information protection controls

AI readiness starts with operational discipline.

⚠️Trust Is a Continuous Process

🔄A common misconception is that evaluating an AI solution is a one-time event.

Traditional software assessments often occur during procurement or onboarding. AI changes that equation because models evolve, behavior shifts, and outputs can change over time. Even without major updates, model performance may drift.

Haupt compared AI trust to a credit score. A high score today does not guarantee future performance. Trust must be continually monitored, measured, and maintained.

Organizations should think of AI not as a static technology purchase but as a living product that requires ongoing governance and oversight. 📈

📉Why Many AI Investments Struggle to Deliver Value

💭Despite massive investment across industries, many organizations are still struggling to achieve meaningful returns from AI initiatives.

Several factors contribute to this challenge:

  • 🔄Perpetual pilot programs with unclear success criteria
  • 📏Limited understanding of how to measure AI-driven outcomes
  • 💲Rapidly evolving pricing models
  • 🎯Unrealistic expectations about what AI can accomplish immediately

Many companies are still learning how to define appropriate metrics for productivity, quality improvements, and business impact. Until those measurements mature, proving ROI will remain difficult.

🏁The Future Belongs to Organizations That Prioritize Trust

🌟As AI becomes increasingly embedded into enterprise operations, procurement, security, and business teams must work together more closely than ever before.

Success will require smarter contracts, stronger governance, clearer accountability, and a shared understanding of risk. Most importantly, organizations must recognize that AI behaves less like traditional software and more like a digital worker capable of making mistakes. That reality demands oversight, transparency, and trust. 🤝

🔐The takeaway is simple but powerful: The winners of the AI era will not be the organizations that move the fastest. They will be the organizations that build the most trust while moving forward.

After all, as Haupt aptly summarized, the AI race is an endurance event, not a sprint. 🚀🏆
