entry.title: Navigating Towards the Autonomous Enterprise in Healthcare
entry.content:
SAP's latest Business AI innovations from Joule Work and Joule Studio to the Business Data Cloud and what they mean for healthcare organizations transforming at scale. 

Healthcare is at an inflection point. Clinical and operational teams face mounting pressure to do more with less yet most AI deployments remain stuck in pilot mode, unable to scale.  

Recently, we had the privilege of hosting an immersive onsite workshop for our Healthcare partners, where we unveiled SAP's transformative vision for the Autonomous Enterprise and demonstrated how partners can accelerate their AI journey using cutting-edge SAP technologies with an early sneak peak of SAP Joule work including Joule Studio along with some exciting hands-on sessions by building own agents with SAP Joule Studio.

CONTEXT 

Why Most AI Efforts Stall Before They Scale 

Across industries including healthcare the story is frustratingly familiar: proofs of concept that never reach production, AI tools layered on top of disconnected systems, and results that cannot be traced or audited. SAP's research surfaces three structural gaps that keep AI locked in pilot mode: 

  • Lack of Business & Process Context - Generic models can read your data. They cannot reason over how a healthcare organization actually runs from patient admission to reimbursement. 
  • Disconnected Data & Integration - AI is added on top of fragmented, outdated systems. Without a unified data foundation, every insight is incomplete, and every recommendation is unreliable. 
  • Lack of Governance & Reliability - AI that cannot be audited or controlled is a liability especially in regulated environments such as healthcare. 74% of organizations remain stuck in pilot mode. 

"Most AI providers are building from the outside in layering intelligence on top of systems they don't own, data they didn't generate, processes they've never run." 

SAP's response is to build from the inside out. With 50 years of embedded process and industry intelligence, a semantically rich business data model spanning 7.3 million data fields, and enterprise-grade governance covering 100% of AI workloads through ISO 42001, SAP already has the foundation that other providers cannot replicate quickly.  

VISION  

The Autonomous Enterprise: People Direct, Assistants coordinates and Agents Executes 

SAP's architectural north star is the Autonomous Enterprise, a model where people set strategic direction, and AI agents handle routine transactions end to end. In healthcare, this means administrators focus on decisions that matter while intelligent agents manage the operational burden of scheduling, billing, supply chain coordination, and compliance monitoring.  

PRODUCT STRATEGY 

SAP Healthcare Product Strategy 

Verticalization, Billing and EMR-Integration, and Industry AI for Healthcare Providers. 

Our healthcare product strategy rests on several interconnected themes, all delivered in close collaboration with our partner ecosystem. A central pillar is the verticalization of the SAP Autonomous Suite to address the specific needs of healthcare. Building on this foundation, we are enabling trusted partners to deliver the next generation of patient administration and accounting solutions, supported by viable transition paths that are already in place and ongoing localization efforts. In parallel, we are working closely with EMR vendors to establish modern, process-oriented integration. Underpinning all of these efforts, we are advancing AI innovation across the ecosystem - making healthcare data accessible through SAP Business Data Cloud and delivering verticalized AI Assistants and Agents purpose-built for the industry. 

For detailed information on the product strategy for healthcare, check out the blog by Thorsten Kampp here.  

PRODUCT HIGHLIGHTS 

Joule Work — Beyond Chat 

One place to direct the business. Less navigation. Faster action. Better decisions. 

In healthcare, transitioning to AI is not easy. Hence, SAP joule work as a part of the Business AI platform is making the transformation smooth. Joule Work represents a fundamental shift in how enterprise users interact with SAP systems. Rather than switching between applications to find context, complete tasks, or surface insights, users stay in a single workspace. AI assistants bring the context. Agents move the work. People make the decisions that matter. 

"AI does the busy work, so you do your best work." 

For healthcare organizations, this translates directly into reduced administrative burden. A clinical operations manager can query patient scheduling data, trigger a supply order, and review compliance alerts, all in one conversation, accessible on any device without having to navigate between multiple systems. 

Key Capabilities of Joule Work 

  • Conversations - The natural-language interface where healthcare users direct the work. Conversations bring role-based intents, multi-turn threads, typeahead, and auto-suggestions into a single surface that reaches across the SAP Business Suite, so a clinical operations manager can ask about scheduling in SuccessFactors, open supply orders in S/4HANA Cloud, and cross-system status in one thread without switching applications. Responses adapt to what the user actually needs: tables and charts when the answer is data, structured cards when the next step is an action, plain summaries when the user is orienting. On mobile, Conversations run with voice mode on iOS and Android, which matters for clinicians moving between wards rather than sitting at a workstation.  
    Conversations is the most mature part of Joule Work today and is what the first EAC cohort, joining from July onward on SAP-managed Joule and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, will experience first. Over the EAC window, Conversations will progressively unlock deeper cross-system reasoning and richer response formats as more capabilities and agents come online, giving healthcare organizations a way to introduce AI to their teams on familiar ground before layering in more autonomous behavior.

  • Spaces - Spaces help users assemble dynamic workspaces. Rather than navigating to a Fiori app, hunting for the right tile, and stitching context together manually, the user expresses intent and Joule generates a Space: a set of adaptive cards drawn live from the underlying systems, arranged into sections, refreshable, and persisted so the user can come back to the same context later. 
     
    A discharge coordinator asking for "a workspace for ward 4B this afternoon" gets bed availability, pending orders, pharmacy statuses, and transport bookings composed into one view. A procurement lead asking about a supplier gets open POs, delivery estimates, and returns in one place. The Space is generated for that person and that intent, not pre-designed by IT. 

    Spaces is the newest surface in Joule Work, and the EAC window is where healthcare organizations get to experience it first. Cards are generated on demand, refined in place through further prompting, and refreshed against live data through SAP Knowledge Graphs, giving users a single governed surface to reason over information that today lives across separate applications. As the EAC progresses, Spaces will grow richer, with more collaborative and interactive patterns on the roadmap, opening up healthcare-specific extension opportunities for partners both in the shape of the Spaces users receive and in the agents that populate them. 

  • Joule Studio  - Joule Studio helps teams build governed AI agents faster, using business context, reusable agents, and Low-code development. A unified, AI-first development environment for creating agents, apps, and workflows. 

    Building custom AI solutions that actually work in production requires more than a capable language model. It requires deep business context, governed runtimes, and tools that reduce the gap between business intent and working code. Joule Studio delivers exactly that a development environment where healthcare partners and customers can build or extend, SAP-grounded agentic solutions. 

Intent-Based Development: From Idea to Production 

The defining innovation in Joule Studio is intent-based development (IBD) with the ability to describe a desired business outcome in plain language and have AI generate a complete, enterprise-ready solution. The process flows through five stages: 

  1. Business Intent Analysis Describe the business problem in natural language. Joule Studio enriches it with SAP Signavio process context, SAP LeanIX landscape data. SAP Domain Models & SAP Knowledge Graph 
  2. Product Requirements Document (PRD) AI generates a structured PRD anchored in real-world business context, SAP domain models, and the Knowledge Graph. 
  3. The PRD is translated into a technical specification that defines scope, architecture, integrations, and security so implementation is guided not guessed. 
  4. Code Generation & Testing - SAP-aware code is generated from the spec. Automated validation and agent evaluations run behavioral checks before promotion to production. 
  5. Deployment & Governance Solutions deploy to an SAP-managed runtime. The SAP AI Agent Hub provides centralized lifecycle management, observability, and security controls.  

The SAP Advantage in Joule Studio 

  • Unmatched Business Context - Grounded in your technology landscape, applications, processes & best practices. 
  • One Solution, Any Tool - Build agents, apps, or workflows using any tool or framework from low-code to full IDE pro-code in a single environment. 
  • Design-time tooling is free included in BTPEA, CPEA or PAYG entitlements. Runtime promotion available through December 2026 at no additional charge. 

Did we spark your interest in Joule Studio? If yes, check out the demo. 

In addition to web version, Joule Work will be available to Partner and Customers in two further version.  

Joule Work Desktop - Joule Work Desktop brings conversational AI directly to knowledge workers working with your local files, connecting to SAP and non-SAP systems via MCP tools, and automating repetitive tasks through custom Skills, all within a secure environment.

Joule Work Mobile  - Available on iOS and Android with voice mode. Consistent experience across all SAP applications through standalone and embedded Joule modes. 

Healthcare-Relevant Agents 

Recent AI Agents and AI features capabilities shipped for by SAP could also be adapted and extended by Healthcare Industry as per the need. Joule Studio enables partners to build and extend agents covering the full care and operations continuum. Examples from existing AI Agents and Features relevant to healthcare: 

  • Supplier Delivery Date Prediction 
  • Catalog item recommendations 
  • AI-Assisted Forecasting,  
  • Automatic Outlier Correction,  
  • Conversational Planning, and so on 

Supplier Delivery Date Prediction, an AI-powered capability available in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. 

The goal of this functionality is straightforward: instead of relying solely on the delivery date promised by a supplier, SAP uses historical purchasing data and machine learning to predict when a purchase order is actually likely to arrive. This gives procurement teams a more realistic view of expected deliveries and allows them to act before delays become a problem. 

For hospitals, this can provide significant operational value. Hospitals depend on the timely delivery of thousands of products every day from pharmaceuticals and medical consumables to implants, laboratory supplies, and spare parts for critical medical equipment. 

If the system predicts that a delivery is likely to be late, procurement teams can proactively contact the supplier, source an alternative product, or adjust inventory plans before patient care is affected. This shifts the organization from reacting to supply issues after they occur to managing them proactively. 

From a business perspective, the benefits include improved delivery accuracy, better planning, and more informed purchasing decisions. It can also help reduce emergency purchases, minimize stock shortages, and improve supplier performance over time. 

Overall, this capability helps hospital procurement teams make smarter, data-driven decisions, improve supply chain resilience, and ultimately support better patient care through more reliable material availability. 
 
By providing early visibility into supplier risks, hospitals can reduce disruptions, improve inventory planning, and ensure that critical medical supplies are available when clinicians need them most." 

Find out more on the released AI Agents and Features in the Discovery Center. 

Get Started with the Joule Studio and Register to stay updated with the latest information on Joule Studio. 

SAP Business Data Cloud — The Data Foundation for AI 

Centralizing business data for seamless integration, analytics, and AI-supported processes in healthcare 

Healthcare organizations have invested heavily in data infrastructure warehouses, lakes, analytics platforms yet most were optimized for dashboards in a deterministic world. The AI era demands a Knowledge Core: constantly connected, context-rich data that intelligent agents can reason over. SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) is that foundation bringing together SAP and non-SAP data under a unified semantic layer, grounding it in the SAP Knowledge Graph, and making it available to Joule agents and intelligent applications. 

Healthcare Data Strategy in BDC - Looking ahead, SAP plans to make health-related data from both SAP and non-SAP source systems available within Business Data Cloud. This creates a single, governed data environment where healthcare-specific analytics, AI agents, and operational reporting all draw from the same authoritative source: patient-to-reimbursement analytics, bed utilization dashboards, and workforce planning all connected, semantically enriched, and AI-ready. 

Are you interested in more details on how BDC could accelerate your journey to AI? Check out the blog post by Shashank Goyal. 

SUMMARY 

What This Means for Healthcare Partners? 

The partner enablement session made one message unmistakably clear: SAP's healthcare AI strategy is not a collection of standalone features; it is a cohesive architecture built for the Autonomous Enterprise. For ecosystem partners building on SAP, the opportunity is significant: 

  • Build with Confidence - Joule Studio provides a governed, AI-first environment to build healthcare-specific agents and apps grounded in SAP business context not starting from scratch. 
  • Leverage a Ready Data Foundation  - BDC's intelligent content, data products, and FHIR-enabled healthcare data layer reduces time to value for analytics and AI use cases substantially. 
  • Deliver Seamless User Experiences - Joule Work app-less, adaptive interface means end users can act on AI-driven insights without navigating complex application landscapes. 
  • Operate in a Governed Environment - The SAP AI Agent Hub provides centralized lifecycle management, observability, and security controls for all deployed agents essential in regulated healthcare settings. 

 "When conditions change, the business acts as one. Agents coordinate across the business in real time. No lag between signal and action." 

Healthcare's next chapter is being written now by those bold enough to build it. The platform is ready. The ecosystem is here. The question is: are you in? 

We would love to hear from our partners and customers. Whether you are exploring your first AI use case, looking to extend an existing solution, or ready to build the next breakthrough for healthcare providers, reach out directly and let's continue the conversation and build modern healthcare together.

entry.title: Connecting a Custom MCP Server to Joule Work Desktop: A Seamless and Secure Authentication Flow
entry.content:
Joule Work Desktop, expected to reach General Availability (GA) in Q3-Q4 2026, serves as SAP's standalone client for enterprise AI assistance. While it provides out-of-the-box integrations, its primary extensibility mechanism relies on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP enables developers to expose data and actions from custom BTP applications—such as those built with CAPM and Node.js on Cloud Foundry—directly to the LLM as callable tools.

From an end-user perspective, connecting an MCP server to Joule requires nothing more than pasting a URL. However, this simple interaction initiates a full OAuth 2.0 handshake designed to enforce enterprise security using the organization's existing Single Sign-On (SSO) infrastructure.

This post outlines the authentication architecture required to connect a custom BTP application securely to Joule Work Desktop.

Interactive vs. Machine-to-Machine Authentication

Enterprise MCP servers must handle different authentication patterns depending on the caller:

  • Interactive Flow (Authorization Code + PKCE): Required when a human employee connects Joule Work Desktop to the MCP server. This flow relies on the user's personal identity established through corporate SSO.

  • Machine-to-Machine (Client Credentials): Used for automated processes, such as scheduled jobs or integration tests, where administrators provision technical service accounts.

For Joule Work Desktop integrations exposing custom BTP data, the interactive flow is required.

The Interactive Flow Architecture

When a user registers an MCP server URL in Joule, the client executes a multi-step handshake.

Phase A: Dynamic Client Registration

Joule must first acquire unique credentials from the custom BTP application.

  • Joule sends a POST request to the server's /register endpoint to request a client_id and client_secret.

  • This exchange follows the RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration standard.

  • While registration is open, the generated credentials remain completely inactive until a legitimate employee completes SSO authorization.

Phase B: SSO Login and Auto-Approval

This is the only interactive step for the user, establishing identity and verifying role assignments.

  • Joule opens a browser window targeting the server's /authorize endpoint.

  • The server detects the missing session and redirects the browser to the organization's identity provider, such as IAS or Corporate IDP through SAP XSUAA.

  • Following a successful SSO login, the identity provider returns an authorization code, which the MCP server exchanges for a signed user identity token containing the user's role claims.

  • The server verifies the user holds the required roles to access the custom BTP application.

  • If the role check passes, the server activates the pending client record created in Phase A, binds it to the authenticated user, and generates a short-lived authorization code.

Phase C: Token Exchange with PKCE

Joule now trades the authorization code for standard OAuth tokens.

  • Joule issues a POST to the /token endpoint with the authorization code and a Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE) code_verifier.

  • The server confirms the authorization code is valid, the client credentials match, and the PKCE verifier hashes exactly to the challenge provided during Phase B.

  • This PKCE validation ensures that intercepted authorization codes cannot be used without the original verifier held by Joule.

  • The server then issues an opaque access token and a refresh token.

Phase D :  Forwarding Identity to the Backend

With authentication complete, Joule executes MCP tool calls against the BTP application.

  • Every request Joule sends to the /mcp endpoint includes the access token within a Bearer header.

  • The MCP server validates the token and resolves it to the specific user identity established during Phase B.

  • The MCP server forwards the tool request to the underlying BTP backend using the caller's actual identity assertion.

Visualizing the Secure Handshake

MCP Authorization Flow from MCP

Security and Authorization Advantages

Exposing custom BTP application data via this MCP architecture ensures that LLM access respects existing enterprise security models.

  • Single Authorization Pipeline: By forwarding the user's identity assertion, the BTP backend executes the exact same authorization logic it uses for standard web UIs. There is no separate permission model to maintain.

  • Enforced Data Filtering: Row-level data access restrictions are applied directly at the backend database. The MCP server never receives unfiltered data, preventing the LLM from accessing unauthorized records.

  • Immediate Revocation: Access tokens trace directly back to the human identity. If an administrator modifies a user's roles in XSUAA, those changes propagate automatically during the next token refresh, instantly revoking unauthorized MCP access.

Note: The architecture and authentication flow detailed above represent a tentative baseline. This flow is flexible and can be modified to align with specific organizational security policies, existing identity provider configurations, and custom customer requirements.

entry.title: From Predictions to Real Decisions: How SAP RPT-1.5 and Joule Agents Orchestrate AI Workflows
entry.content:
Orchestrating Joule with Joule Agents powered by SAP RPT Model

With the launch of SAP's very own Foundation Model: SAP-RPT-1.5, decision making now becomes way easier with accurate predictions available at your fingertips within Joule. 

We built an AI workflow where a purpose-built tabular prediction model (RPT-1.5) works hand-in-hand with an AI agents embedded in SAP Joule to turn structured shipment data into real-time logistics decisions - no dashboard-staring required, no ABAP queries, worklists, custom enhancements to maintain business rules.  This article shows how we did it, what we learned, and how the pattern generalizes to any enterprise decision driven by structured data.

The real value of AI agents comes from orchestrating them around high-quality structured data and well-defined decisions.

Structured Data Remains Your Most Powerful AI Asset

Large language models excel at unstructured text. But enterprise decisions - invoice late payments, inventory reorder points, supplier risk scoring - depend on structured, tabular data: order histories, rate tables, lead times, weights, distances, and transit durations.

This data has properties that make it uniquely valuable for AI:

  • Auditable: Every prediction traces back to specific rows and columns.
  • High-signal: A structured order history encodes patterns no prompt can replicate.
  • Real-time: ERP data updates continuously - predictions must reflect the latest state.
  • Governed: Enterprises already have data quality, lineage, and access controls in place.
  • Explainability: Predictions comes with closest comparables that led to the result values and confidence levels.

The challenge is that general-purpose LLMs struggle with tabular reasoning. Keeping the token cost aside, they hallucinate column names, miscalculate aggregations, and cannot learn from hundreds of historical examples in a single prompt window. This is precisely why we launched our foundation model - SAP-RPT-1.5 and invested in Tabular AI with Prior Lab's TabPFN Models.

Introducing RPT-1.5: A few-shot Tabular Pre-Trained Model

RPT (Relational Pre-Trained Transformer model) is SAP's purpose-built model for tabular in-context learning. Unlike general LLMs that treat tables as text, RPT-1.5 natively understands table structure - columns, data types, relationships between features - through specialized table embeddings. 

How RPT-1.5 Works

RPT-1.5 performs in-context learning on tabular data. You pass it a DataFrame of historical examples along with a new row containing [PREDICT] placeholders or missing fields in existing data with [PREDICT] placeholders, and it returns predictions with confidence scores - no fine-tuning, no feature engineering, no preprocessing pipeline.

Sample Context + Query with RPT output

Attribute

SAP-RPT-1.5 Model

 Architecture

 Transformer with specialized table embeddings

 Input

 Raw tabular data (ERP data)

 Output

 Classification probabilities or regression predictions

 Context Window

 8192 tokens (adaptive batching)

 Training Data

 Large-scale real-world data

 Key Innovation

 Column names + cell values embedded via LLM-style tokenization

 Deployment

 SAP AI Core GenAI Hub (cloud)


Enabling RPT-1.5 model in AI Core - Step by step guide

What RPT-1.5 Predicts in Our Use Case

For transportation order management, RPT-1.5 simultaneously predicts:

  • Optimal Carrier (FEDEX, UPS etc.): classification with confidence score
  • Shipping Rate (in local currency): regression with confidence interval
  • Transit Duration (hours): regression for delivery time estimation

The model achieves ≥95% carrier prediction accuracy and ≤5% Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) on rate predictions, input of of over 10K+ historical transportation orders spanning multiple carriers, routes, and service levels.

The Agent Workflow: From User Intent to Decision

A prediction model sitting behind an API endpoint is necessary but insufficient. The real value emerges when you embed it in a workflow that connects user intent → data retrieval → prediction → recommendation → action. This is where Joule agents come in.

The Workflow Step by Step

  • User Intent: A logistics coordinator asks Joule: "Predict carrier and rate for 150 pounds from Houston to Boston." The RPT Prediction scenario uses direct scenario trigger to intercept this and extract slots: shipper=Houston, consignee=Boston, weight=150, prediction_type=both.
  • Historical Context Assembly: The capability assembles 10K+ diverse historical transportation orders as in-context learning(ICL) rows, covering different carriers, routes, weights, and service levels. These are the "context rows" the model used for in-context learning for reasoning over at inference time.

The RPT-1.5 Powered Workflow

With our Joule agent + RPT-1.5 integration:

  1. Coordinator creates a shipment of 320 LB, Boston → Miami, Transportation Mode: Air. Asks Joule to display the transportation trends for the last quarter (Zero cold start).
    RPT Trend Analysis

  2. User then asks Joule to predict the carrier for a future shipment. 
    RPT Predictions in Joule

  3. Joule instantly surfaces a prediction card: "Predicted Carrier: DHL (81% confidence), Predicted Rate: $595 (92% confidence)"
    Prediction results in Joule UI5 Card

  4. The transit time prediction is based on 10K+ historical orders - encoding seasonal patterns, carrier performance by route, weight-based pricing, and service-level agreements. 
    Transit Times Comparisons by RPT in Joule

  5. Coordinator continues to predict carrier and rate for more transportation routes. 
    Multiple Predictions in single RPT call

  6. Decision time: <30 seconds (from 15-25 minutes) within SAP Build Work Zone or Joule Work Mobile
    RPT Predictions in Joule with Build Work Zone
    RPT Predictions in Joule Work Mobile

The Impact at Scale

Metric

Before (Manual)

After (RPT-1.5 + Joule)

Decision Time per Order

15-25 minutes

<30 seconds

Carrier Selection Accuracy

~78% (vs. optimal)

≥95% (vs. optimal)

Rate Prediction Error

±12-15%

≤5% MAPE

Orders Processed/Day/Person

~40

~500+

Annual Freight Savings (1000 orders/week)

Baseline

8-12% cost reduction


Key Learnings

Our implementation taught us that successful enterprise AI agent workflows require four distinct layers:

Layer 1: Data and Semantic Layer

The foundation is high-quality, governed structured data. In our case: 100K+ transportation orders from SAP system with standardized column names, consistent units, and complete lineage. The S/4HANA system provides real-time access via OData APIs with principal propagation (SSO) ensuring data sovereignty, the agent only fetches the data the logged-in user is authorized to access.

Layer 2: Tabular Prediction Layer (RPT-1.5)

The specialized model that understands tables natively. RPT-1.5's in-context learning approach means no retraining when routes or carriers change - you simply update the historical context rows. The model is deployed on SAP AI Core with a dedicated inference endpoint, or optionally on NVIDIA DGX Spark using the sap-rpt-1-oss on Hugging Face.

Layer 3: Orchestration and Tools (Joule Capability Framework)

The Joule capability framework (SAP DAS) provides the orchestration layer - connecting user intent to model inference to action. Our RPT Prediction Capability defines:

  • Scenarios: predict_shipment, predict_rate, predict_transit_time, show_trends
  • Functions: predict_carrier_rate (core), predict_with_live_data (ERP-enriched)
  • System Aliases: AICORE_RPT_MODEL (model deployment endpoint), S/4 system (live data)
  • Slot Extraction: Natural language → structured parameters (origin, destination, weight, prediction_type)

Layer 4: Experience Layer (Joule UI)

The final layer is how recommendations reach the user. Joule renders prediction results as interactive UI5 cards with confidence scores, optional action buttons (Accept, Override, Run Again), and contextual follow-ups. The user never leaves their workflow - predictions can be made to appear inline within your S/4HANA system or Fiori Apps or even remain with Joule Conversations. 

How to Get Started

A practical checklist for building your first tabular AI agent workflow:

  1. Identify a decision-making use case that requires predictions (classification or regression), forecasting, trend analysis. 
  2. Evaluate your test data and prediction results using RPT Playground
  3. Deploy SAP-RPT-1.5 in your AI Core instance. Refer to the Step-by-Step Guide
  4. Build a Joule capability to orchestrate the scenario selection, invoking RPT model and displaying predicted results. 
  5. Design the output from RPT to a target UI to enable users' in decision-making - UI5 Cards in Joule, Fiori Apps, etc. 
  6. Automate invoking the Joule Agents from ABAP layer using A2A.

Conclusion

Orchestration is what turns structured data into continuous, trusted decisions at scale. SAP-RPT-1.5 enables tabular prediction superpowers. Joule agents give us workflow integrations. Together, they transform business users' decision-making from "pull data, stare at dashboard, decide" to "ask question, get recommendation, act."

The win doesn't come from having the best model. It comes from embedding AI into real business processes as we did with carrier selection, rate negotiation, shipment optimization and then iterating over a automated workflow that update the historical context in real-time. This enable RPT results to always calculate on latest shipments executed in the real world without any training. 

Jump start your journey with our comprehensive repository with sample request, simply download the repository and customize it with your context data. Happy Predicting! 🚀

entry.title: Joule Work on the Go and Mobile Design System Enhancements: What's New in SAP's Mobile Experience
entry.content:
In the first half of this year, SAP Fiori for Android and SAP Fiori for iOS as well as Joule mobile client have undergone a series of intelligent improvements aimed at elevating user experience and boosting productivity. These enhancements have introduced greater flexibility, consistency, and functionality across both platforms, ensuring that users can navigate their applications with ease and efficiency.

On top of that, the Joule Work app, formerly known as SAP Mobile Start, has been introduced at SAP Sapphire. With this app, complex tasks can be accomplished while on the go. Users simply need to define their goals and let AI take action.

 

Joule Work Mobile App

Joule Work is a central, intelligent workspace where AI takes charge of the busy work, enabling users to focus on driving outcomes. It transforms the work environment with a proactive, outcome-driven experience, where users articulate goals and AI coordinates actions across systems to accomplish them efficiently. Processes speed up considerably with proactive assistance, using the comprehensive business context of Joule Agents and Joule Assistants to highlight relevant data and suggest actions. This setup streamlines complexity, allowing users to focus on decision-making and outcome generation, while routine tasks are delegated to supervised agents. In addition to the web app, Joule Work offers a desktop app for faster access to local files and applications, as well as a mobile app for managing complex workflows on the go.

Conversations

Conversations act as dynamic interfaces for seamless interaction with Joule, making engagement intuitive and natural. Users can easily express their needs by typing, speaking, or attaching files, eliminating the need for traditional navigation methods. Joule enriches this process by offering context-based prompts, conducting platform-wide searches, and providing detailed answers with real-time data and interactive elements. By facilitating dialogue, conversations enable users to express their intentions and explore desired outcomes, drawing together insights and results from SAP and third-party systems. Moreover, conversations serve as entry points to spaces, supporting more complex workflows. This streamlined approach enhances user engagement and simplifies the pursuit of information and task completion.

Spaces

Spaces are dynamic, AI-generated workspaces tailored to match a user's intent, offering a seamless user experience. These adaptable environments allow users to engage in conversations and customize features without navigating through apps or dashboards, ensuring that individual needs are met efficiently. Within a space, tasks can be completed using natural language or structured inputs, fostering intuitive and effective interactions. Spaces are created in real time, pulling together the necessary data, tools, and context to achieve specific goals. They display only essential information through actionable summary cards, tables, metrics, or alerts, enabling users to focus on their tasks without distractions. These persistent spaces ensure users can easily return to continue their work from where they left off, facilitating both simple and complex problem-solving with ease.

Download for Android | Download for iOS

 

Joule mobile client 

The Joule mobile client, which facilitates the integration of Joule into Joule Work, provides exciting new features designed to enhance user interaction and streamline communication. Dictation allows users to harness the power of their device's built-in voice recognition, enabling hands-free messaging and smoother, more accessible conversation workflows with Joule. This innovation is perfect for busy professionals who need to multitask, as it allows them to communicate effortlessly without sacrificing productivity. The newly integrated typeahead feature intelligently offers contextual suggestions as users type. This predictive element cuts down on keystrokes and expedites prompt completion, resulting in more efficient interactions. Alongside these input features, Joule has also expanded its functionality with response actions, enabling users to easily copy or regenerate responses directly within the conversation. This means users can quickly reuse Joule's outputs or request new answers without retyping prompts, offering a seamless, user-friendly experience. Additionally, the transparency and explainability feature has been improved to provide users with clearer insights into Joule's AI-generated replies, ensuring they understand the response origins and details. Sources are now displayed separately from response insights, giving users straightforward access to the information that influences their conversations. Together, these updates demonstrate Joule’s commitment to enhancing user productivity and communication efficiency through innovative solutions while ensuring clarity and confidence in AI interactions.

 

What’s New in SAP Fiori for Android 26.1 and 26.4

Extended Card Header

The extended card header has been updated for greater flexibility, enabling you to place various components, such as tags, status indicators, or custom elements, together in a single row. This allows for more compact, streamlined, and versatile card layouts.

For more information, check out Card Header in the SAP Fiori for Android design guidelines.

Extended card header

Multi-User Onboarding

The user list now reflects SAP Fiori for iOS standards and displays users onboarded to a specific device, sorted from the earliest to the most recent.

For more information, check out Multi-User Onboarding.

Switching or adding a user

Step Progress Indicator

The nodes in the step progress indicator, which is designed to track and display a user's status within a user flow, now offer the same customization options as SAP BTP SDK for iOS. You can modify the size, layout, and icon in an icon node and specify different states for the icon node. When there are just a few steps, the width of each step expands to fill the screen, creating a more balanced layout.

Refer to Step Progress Indicator to find out more about this component.

Step progress indicator

List Picker Form Cell

A read-only state has been added to the list picker form cell, which allows for the selection of one or more options among values within a defined category. In this state, the selected value(s) are shown, and the chevron is removed. The cell height adjusts to ensure that all selected values are displayed without any truncation.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cell

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell, which allows users to turn on/off individual settings, now includes a read-only state. In this state, the toggle switch control is replaced with a text label that indicates the pre-set value. While the default label is “On/Off,” you can customize it to provide more contextual messages, such as "Included/Not Included."

See Switches for more details.

Switch form cell

 

What’s New in iOS 26.1 and 26.4

AI User Feedback

The AI user feedback feature lets users share their experiences with AI. The inline AI feedback entry point has been updated to function as a standalone, reusable component.

See AI User Feedback for more information.

AI inline user feedback

Step Progress Indicator

The step progress indicator, which monitors and shows a user's position within a user flow, has been enhanced. The width of each step node is now adaptable with a set minimum value, allowing the indicator to expand and fill the screen width when there are fewer steps visible.

Explore the Step Progress Indicator.

Step progress indicator nodes

List Picker Form Cell

The list picker now features a read-only state where selected values appear inline, the chevron is removed, and the cell becomes non-interactive. There is no word limit on displayed values. However, lengthy or multi-selected values might cause the cell height to stretch. To address this, we recommend either avoiding the read-only state or implementing a custom summary view.

Learn more about the List Picker Form Cell.

List picker form cells

Switch Form Cell

The switch form cell now includes a read-only state where a text label, defaulting to "On/Off," is shown instead of the visual switch. This label is fully customizable to offer more contextual messaging, such as "Included/Not Included." The form cell height and padding are consistent with the active state, ensuring a seamless layout experience.

Read more about the Switch Form Cell.

Switch form cell

 

UI Kits for Figma

SAP Fiori for Android and iOS UI Kit

With the updated SAP Fiori for Android and iOS UI Kits, it’s now easier than ever to use the latest components and patterns in your mobile design. By using the UI Kits, you can quickly create a consistent user experience that enables app implementations at scale.

SAP Fiori for Android UI Kits | SAP Fiori for iOS UI Kits

entry.title: SAP Joule Work mobile app version 3.2 brings exciting new features
entry.content:
Let's have a look at the new features that got released for both experiences, the Joule Work experience, as well as the SAP Build Work Zone experience – formally called SAP Mobile Start.

Let´s start with the features that are valid for both experiences.

With the latest release, Joule conversations are now shared between mobile and web, meaning you can start a conversation on mobile and then continue it on your laptop or desktop computer. Certainly, also expired conversations will be available on mobile and web.

The new Profile and Settings entry “Conversations” allows you to see your user profile data and to enable/ disable the Joule memory feature right in the mobile app. When turned on, Joule remembers your preferences, workflows, and chat goals to keep responses relevant and fast. Memories are usually kept for 12 months, but you can revoke consent anytime by deactivating its toggle, then the memories are deleted immediately. You can always see the stored data under “Saved Memories”.

 Screenshot: New setting entry for conversations: Memory

You can now engage in natural voice conversations with Joule Work in the mobile app. With the latest release, you can speak directly to Joule and receive spoken responses, eliminating the need to look at your device screen. This hands-free experience is particularly useful when you are on the go or need to work without interacting with your device. The new Apple CarPlay integration also enables you to communicate with Joule while driving—for example, to prepare for your next customer meeting. 

 Screenshot: Joule Work in Apple Carplay

Since the last release, we allow you to customize the Support Section on the "Profile and Settings" screen. This allows you to add additional information for your users, in case they have any support needs. Now, administrators can additionally add free text to this section. Once configured, the info is displayed on the Profile and Settings screen as well as during the onboarding process. The feature can be added and configured via SAP Mobile Services or via Mobile Device Management (MDM) . Please also check our SAP Help documentation for details.

Finally, administrators can select a dedicated browser via MDM for the onboarding process. This feature can be used to define the browser the Joule Work mobile app uses for the initial onboarding authentication and possible re-authentication and allows you to enforce a specific browser policy across your managed device fleet. The setting does not affect the general in-app browsing behavior. 
We also have added Thai to the list of supported languages for SAP Joule mobile app.

Next, let´s have a look at the new feature for only Joule Work experience.

You can now view insights on your spaces and cards. Just tap on the overflow menu (three dots) of a space and select “Open Insights”. Then the insights overlay appears and provides info such as which steps got executed and which sources got leveraged to create the space.

Screenshot: Insights on Spaces

Finally, what is new for SAP Build Work Zone experience?

With the last release we had introduced workspaces for SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition. Since then, you can easily access your workspaces when being away from your desk with the Joule Work mobile app. Now, you can also add your favorite workspaces to the Start screen, with your changes synced automatically across mobile and web. To add a workspace to the Start screen, just do a long tap on a workspace tile and add it – the same way you know from adding app favorites.  

I hope you will enjoy these features in the Joule Work mobile app.

Visit SAP Mobile Experience Community Page and click “follow” to get the latest development and innovation of our solutions. We look forward to hearing about your experience with setting up the solution in your landscape; please do share your thoughts and comments below. Enter here for additional questions regarding SAP Mobile Experience Applications.

Want to be notified? Check your profile settings to ensure you have your settings activated.

entry.title: t's All Joule Everywhere, Do You Actually Know Which Joule You are Talking About?
entry.content:
t's All Joule Everywhere, Do You Actually Know Which Joule You are Talking About?

Spend any time in the SAP ecosystem right now and you will hear one word more than any other and its Joule

Joule in SuccessFactors. Joule Work. Joule Agents. Joule Assistants. Joule Studio. It's on every slide in every keynote, in every product update. 

"Are these all the same thing? Are they different products? What does each one actually do, and which one do I actually need?"

Let's break it down.

Before the classification, it's worth asking: why does this family even exist?

For decades, enterprise software was designed around a fundamental assumption: users learn the system. You train people to navigate menus, find features, run reports, follow workflows. The system was the authority and users adapted to it.

The result? Feature-rich platforms where most users only ever discover 20% of the capability. Time-off requests, performance forms and policy questions are all buried inside screens that require navigation, training and patience.

The Joule Family: A Clear Classification

Think of the Joule family as a layered stack each layer serving a distinct purpose, all working together

Layer 1 — Joule (The Umbrella AI Experience)

What it is: Joule is SAP's overarching AI copilot and engagement layer. It is "the broader AI experience through which people interact with their business.

The need it addresses: Users need a single, consistent AI presence across SAP regardless of which module, which device, or which process they are working in. Joule is that presence.

Its function: Joule answers questions, provides recommendations, helps users navigate to the right application, and surfaces insights drawn from SAP and connected third-party data. It is grounded in the SAP Knowledge Graph, which maps more than 7 million data fields across the SAP portfolio giving it real business context, not generic AI responses.

Layer 2 — Joule Assistants (The Orchestrators)

What they are: Joule Assistants are purpose-built for a specific business role or process. They go beyond answering questions they coordinate the work that needs to happen within a defined business context.

The need they address: Generic AI can answer questions. But HR work is contextual. A payroll query and a workforce planning request are very different they need different data, different logic, different guardrails. Joule Assistants bring that role-specific intelligence.

its function: "The Assistant coordinates the work, while the Agent carries out the tasks needed to move it forward." Assistants understand the nuances of a process, surface the right context

Layer 3 — Joule Agents (The Executors)

What they are: Joule Agents are the doers. They execute multi-step tasks autonomously across systems, across data sources, within the boundaries set by your organisation's existing authorisations, rules and audit trails.

The need they address: Orchestration without execution is just planning. Once an Assistant decides what needs to happen, something has to do it update a record, trigger a workflow, move a configuration, generate a document across potentially multiple systems in sequence.

Their function: Agents carry out specific, bounded tasks. Critically, they operate within your existing governance they don't bypass permissions or create shadow workflows. SAP's framing is deliberate: "Agents operate within established data, authorisations, and audit trails to maintain control."

Layer 4 — Joule Work (The Workspace / UI)

What it is: Joule Work is the new unified interface "the new UI for AI" where employees and HR teams actually engage with all of the above. Launched at SAP Connect 2026 and rolling out to all customers in October 2026.

The need it addresses: Having powerful Assistants and Agents is only useful if people can actually reach them intuitively. Joule Work solves the access and discoverability problem it replaces navigation-first interaction with intent-first interaction.

Its function: Joule Work is built on three pillars:

  • Conversations - Users express what they want in natural language. Joule Work interprets the intent, engages the right Assistant, and gets the work done.
  • Spaces - Dynamic, shared work areas that surface the content, data, insights, and applications relevant to a goal - across SAP and non-SAP sources. Think of a Workforce Planning Space that brings together headcount data, open roles, skills gaps, and budget in one view.
  • Develop (Joule Studio) - The build capability, directly accessible within Joule Work, where teams extend or create their own agents and workflows.

 

Layer 5 — Joule Studio (The Build Layer)

 

What it is: Joule Studio is SAP's AI-first development environment. It enables business users and IT professionals to create, customise and govern AI agents and workflows from no-code to pro-code.

The need it addresses: No out-of-the-box agent library covers every organisation's unique HR processes. Companies need the ability to extend Joule to fit their specific workflows, policies, and data structures without building from scratch on a separate platform.

Its function: Joule Studio lets you describe what you want to build in plain language it translates your intent into product requirements and technical specifications, then helps implement the solution. Agents built in Studio can reason across SAP and non-SAP systems, invoke APIs, and integrate into governed enterprise workflows.

 

How It All Fits Together Here's the mental model that I find most useful:

You INTERACT in     →  Joule Work       (the workspace)

You TALK TO         →  Joule            (the AI experience)

It COORDINATES via  →  Joule Assistants (the orchestrators)

It EXECUTES via     →  Joule Agents     (the doers)

You CUSTOMISE with  →  Joule Studio     (the builder)

entry.title: The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work
entry.content:
The Evolution of the SAP User Interface: From SAP GUI to Fiori to Joule Work

From transactions to intuitive apps to AI-powered collaboration – the SAP user experience is not just changing its appearance. It is changing the way we work.

Anyone who has worked with SAP for a long time will remember it: the classic SAP GUI, countless transaction codes, complex screens, and a user interface that was primarily designed to do one thing – provide functionality.

But the world has changed. And so have our expectations of enterprise software.

Looking back, we can see just how far we have come – and what this evolution means for us as people.

1. SAP GUI – The Era of Transactions

Throughout the 1990s and well beyond, SAP GUI was the central entry point to business processes in countless companies.

The interface was powerful, stable, and designed to support complex business processes. To use SAP efficiently, users had to become familiar with transaction codes, screens, fields, and process logic.

People had to learn how SAP worked.

Over the years, experienced users developed an enormous amount of knowledge. They knew which transaction to use, which fields mattered, and which steps were required to achieve the desired result.

It worked – but shift began in the design of the user experience.

Instead of complex transaction screens, the focus moved towards role-based apps, modern design, and more intuitive interaction. The user experience became increasingly aligned with people's tasks and needs.

Information was meant to be easier to access. Processes were meant to become more understandable. And SAP was increasingly expected to feel as intuitive as the modern applications we use in everyday life.

The key question changed: Not just “How does this transaction work?” but “What task do I want to accomplish?”

With Fiori, access to SAP became more modern, flexible, and better suited to different roles and devices.

This was more than a new design. It was an important step towards a better user experience and a stronger focus on people.

3. Joule Work – From Using Software to AI-Powered Collaboration

With generative AI, the next chapter of the SAP user experience is beginning.

AI assistants such as Joule make it possible to ask for information in natural language, understand relationships more quickly, and receive intelligent support when completing certain tasks.

With Joule Work, SAP is taking this approach further towards an AI-powered work environment. The aim is to bring information and work contexts together more effectively and support tasks across different applications and business processes.

Instead of navigating exclusively through menus and applications, users can increasingly describe what they want to achieve.

Imagine a typical business scenario:

Instead of opening multiple reports and manually compiling data, a user could ask:

“Analyze sales performance over the past three months, identify the largest deviations, and summarize the most important areas for action.”

The vision is for AI to help users find information, analyze data, and prepare decisions – and, depending on available capabilities and permissions, also assist in executing tasks.

People will spend less time searching for information and more time interpreting it and making the right decisions.

An important point: Not every task can already be fully automated. The actual benefits depend on the available capabilities, integration with business processes, and the quality of the underlying data.

4. The Real Change Is About People

The evolution of the SAP user interface is therefore not just a story about technology.

It is also a story about how our work is changing.

Era What matters most What it means for people

SAP GUITransactions and screensSystem knowledge and process expertise are essential
SAP FioriApps and tasksMore intuitive interaction and easier access to information
Joule Work and AIIntent, context, and assistanceGreater focus on analysis, decisions, and collaboration

This evolution raises important questions.

Which skills will become more important in the future?

Knowledge of individual transactions will remain valuable in many areas. At the same time, other skills will become increasingly important: asking the right questions, critically evaluating results, understanding business processes, and using AI effectively.

The roles of IT departments, SAP consultants, and process owners are also changing. It is no longer just about configuring systems correctly and training users. Increasingly, it is about designing intelligent workflows, making meaningful use of data, and helping people adapt to a new world of work.

And this is where a major challenge lies: New technology alone does not change the way people work. Real value is created only when people understand, trust, and use it effectively.

5. What Does This Mean for SAP Transformations?

For companies, one important insight emerges: The evolution of the user interface should not be treated as an isolated IT project.

Organizations modernizing SAP should also rethink their workflows, employee roles, data quality, and opportunities for automation.

Some key questions to consider:

  • Which tasks can be simplified through better user experience and guidance?

  • Where can AI assistants make information available more quickly?

  • Which processes are suitable for further automation?

  • How can we ensure that employees understand and embrace the new possibilities?

  • How do we measure whether productivity, quality, and employee satisfaction are actually improving?

Especially in the SAP ecosystem, it will be crucial to develop technology, processes, and people together.

Because a modern interface is not an end in itself. It must make work easier, better, and more meaningful.

Conclusion: Less Time Operating Systems. More Time Making an Impact.

From SAP GUI through SAP Fiori to Joule Work, we are witnessing an evolution that goes far beyond the design of a user interface.

We are moving from a world where people had to learn how to operate the system, through a world of intuitive, task-oriented applications, towards a way of working in which AI increasingly understands, assists, and supports tasks.

The exciting question is therefore no longer just what the next SAP interface will look like.

The real question is: How much more can people achieve when technology takes some of the complexity off their shoulders?

The future of SAP will not be measured solely by how intelligent the systems become. It will be measured by how effectively they help people make better decisions, collaborate more efficiently, and focus on what truly matters.

Less complexity. More intelligence. More time for what really matters.

entry.title: SAP CPQ : The Future of Sales Quoting Is Here: Meet SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant & Other Agents
entry.content:
Disclaimer: : The purpose of this blog is to share a custom implementation approach for automating sales processes in SAP CPQ using Joule Work and Joule Studio. This content is aimed at customers and partners interested in innovation and automation scenarios.  
If you would like to explore these capabilities, please enroll in the EAC program and connect with your SAP CSM, CSP, or Account Executive to discuss available options.

Also please watch out for the Official SAP CPQ Product Roadmap items for Joule Assistants Delivery and What's New for SAP CPQ releases time to time.

How AI is transforming one of sales' most time-consuming processes

Every sales rep knows the pain. A customer sends over an email — or a ten-page PDF — and suddenly you're spending the better part of your afternoon manually parsing the request, matching products, checking pricing rules, and assembling a proposal document. It's repetitive, error-prone, and it gets in the way of actual selling.

SAP's Joule Quoting Assistant & remaining 6 other Agents is designed to change that entirely.

What Is the Joule Quoting Assistant?

The Joule Quoting Assistant is an AI-powered Joule Assistant — part of SAP's broader agentic AI portfolio — built specifically for the quote-to-order cycle. Its core mission: transform unstructured customer requests into accurate, compliant quotes with AI-guided selling across the entire SAP CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) flow. Source

It sits at the intersection of SAP CPQ, SAP Sales Cloud, and SAP S/4HANA, orchestrating specialized AI agents behind the scenes to handle tasks that would otherwise fall to the sales rep or a back-office support team.

From Inbox to Quote: What It Actually Does

Here's where the Quoting Assistant gets practical. Given an unstructured customer inquiry — whether it arrives as an email, a request for quotation (RFQ), or a PDF — the assistant can:

  • Convert the raw request into a structured CPQ quote draft, extracting relevant intent and mapping it to your product catalog and pricing rules.
  • Recommend compliant product configurations based on what the customer described in natural language — no need to manually navigate complex configurators.
  • Surface real-time upsell, add-on, and cross-sell options guided by historical deal data and pricing policies.
  • Assemble proposal documents and draft customer-facing emails, ready for the rep to review and send.
  • Route multi-step requests to the right specialized agents automatically, without manual handoffs.
  • Enforce pricing and discount policies — every quote stays within guardrails, reducing approvals overhead and compliance risk. Source

Why This Matters for your Sales Teams

The shift from manual quoting to AI-guided quoting isn't just about speed — it changes the quality and consistency of the entire sales conversation.

Faster time to first draft. Instead of spending hours building a quote from scratch, reps get an intelligent draft that's already shaped by the customer's actual request. That frees them up to focus on relationship management and deal strategy.

Better accuracy and compliance. When pricing rules, discount limits, and configuration constraints are embedded in the assistant's reasoning, errors are caught before they reach the customer — not after an internal audit.

Higher deal size through guided selling. Real-time upsell and cross-sell recommendations aren't an afterthought; they're built into the quoting flow. Reps are prompted with relevant options at exactly the right moment.

Tighter SAP ecosystem integration. The Quoting Assistant works natively within SAP CPQ and SAP S/4HANA, which means no data re-entry, clean-core alignment, and full traceability across the quote lifecycle. Source

The Architecture Behind It: Assistants + Agents

The Quoting Assistant doesn't work alone. It's part of SAP's layered AI architecture: Joule Assistants — role-aligned, context-aware AI systems — sit above Joule Agents, which are the task specialists that execute individual steps. Source

You tell the Quoting Assistant what you want to accomplish in plain language. It interprets your intent, pulls in your business context (your CPQ rules, your pricing policies, your customer history), and coordinates the agents doing the actual work. You stay in control; the heavy lifting happens automatically.

This architecture is important because it means the Quoting Assistant isn't a standalone tool — it's part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise vision, where AI handles routine execution so people can focus on decisions that require judgment.

A Real-World Scenario

Imagine a key account manager receives an email from a customer requesting a customised bundle of hardware and professional services across three countries, with specific delivery windows and a tight margin requirement.

Historically, this would take hours — coordinating with product management, pricing, and legal before a quote could even be drafted.

With the Joule Quoting Assistant, the rep pastes (or forwards) the customer email, and the assistant:

  1. Parses the request and maps it to available products and service SKUs.
  2. Checks configuration rules and flags any incompatible options.
  3. Proposes a compliant price structure with margin guardrails.
  4. Recommends a maintenance bundle and a support tier upsell.
  5. Drafts the proposal document and a personalised cover email.

The rep reviews, adjusts, approves. What took half a day now takes minutes.

What This Signals for the Future of Sales

SAP's investment in the Quoting Assistant reflects a broader industry shift: the sales rep of the near future is a reviewer and relationship manager, not a data entry clerk. AI handles the structure; humans handle the nuance.

For organisations running SAP CPQ or SAP Sales Cloud v2, this isn't a distant roadmap item — it's available now, and it integrates with the systems you already have. The question isn't whether to evaluate it; it's how quickly you can get it into the hands of your team.

The SAP Joule Quoting Assistant is part of the SAP Joule Assistants portfolio. Learn more at sap.com/use-cases/joule-assistant/quoting-ai.
